CHAPTER 107
Notice of Public Meetings
107.01   Title; interpretation.
107.02   Definitions.
107.03   Meeting dates of Council.
107.04   Notice of regular and organizational meetings.
107.05   Notice of special meetings.
107.06   Notice to news media of special meetings.
107.07   Notification of discussion of specific types of public business.
107.08   General provisions.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Meetings of public bodies to be open - see Ohio R.C. 121.22
   Disturbing a lawful meeting - see GEN. OFF.
548.05
107.01 TITLE; INTERPRETATION.
   The provisions of this chapter relating to Council meetings shall set the
regular meeting dates of Council and establish rules pursuant to Ohio R.C.
121.22(F), for the purpose of:
   (a)   Establishing a reasonable method for any person to determine the time
and place of all regularly scheduled meetings and the time, place and purpose
of all special meetings;
   (b)   Making provisions for giving advance notice of special meetings to the
news media that have requested notification; and
   (c)   Making provisions for persons to request and obtain reasonable advance
notification of all meetings at which any specific type of public business is
to be discussed.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)
107.02 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   As used in this chapter, the following words shall have the meaning
ascribed to them except as and if the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning:
      (1)   "Clerk" means the Clerk of Council.
      (2)   "Day" means calendar day.
      (3)   "Meeting" means any prearranged discussion of the public business
of Council by a majority of the members of Council.
      (4)   "Oral notification" means notification given orally either in
person or by telephone, directly to the person for whom such notification is
intended, or by leaving an oral message for such person at the address, or, if
by telephone, at the telephone number of such person as shown on the records
kept by the Clerk under these rules.
      (5)   "Post" means to post in an area accessible to the public during the
usual business hours at the office of the Clerk at the following locations:
         A.   Bulletin board at the entrance to Council Chambers.
         B.   Bulletin board at City Hall front entrance.
         C.   Bulletin board at City Hall lobby.
         D.   Office of the Clerk of Council, City Hall.
   A notice identifying the locations at which notifications will be posted
pursuant to these rules shall be published by the Clerk within ten calendar
days after the adoption of these rules.
      (6)   "Published" means published once in a newspaper having a general
circulation in the Municipality, as defined in Ohio R.C. 7.12, except that no
portion of such newspaper need be printed in the Municipality. If at the time
of any such publication there is no such newspaper of general circulation, then
the publication shall be in a newspaper then determined by the Clerk to have
the largest circulation in the Municipality.
      (7)   "Special meeting" means a meeting which is neither a regular
meeting nor an adjournment of a regular or special meeting to another time or
day to consider items specifically stated on the original agenda of such
regular or special meeting.
      (8)   "Written notification" means notification in writing mailed,
telegraphed or delivered to the address of the person for whom such
notification is intended as shown on the records kept by the Clerk under these
rules, or in any way delivered to such person. If mailed, such notification
shall be mailed by first-class mail, deposited in a U.S. Postal Service mailbox
no later than the second day preceding the day of the meeting to which such
notification refers, provided that at least one regular mail delivery day falls
between the day of mailing and the day of such meeting.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)
107.03 MEETING DATES OF COUNCIL.
   The regular meeting dates of Council are hereby determined to be the first
and third Mondays of each and every calendar month and which regular Council
meetings may be held at 7:00 p.m. of the prevailing time in the Council
Chambers, City Hall, Painesville, Ohio or any other location within the City of
Painesville as designated by the City Council in accordance with Section
107.04 on the following day. In the event either the first or third Monday of
any calendar month falls upon a legal holiday, the regular Council meeting so
falling on such legal holiday shall be held at 7:00 p.m. on the following day.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76; Ord. 21-11. Passed 5-2-11; Ord. 19-23. Passed 10-2-
23.)
107.04 NOTICE OF REGULAR AND ORGANIZATIONAL MEETINGS.
   (a)   The Clerk shall post a statement of the time(s) and place(s) of
regular meetings of Council for each calendar year not later than the second
day preceding the day of the first regular meeting, other than the
organizational meeting, of the calendar year. The Clerk shall check at
reasonable intervals to ensure that the statement remains so posted during the
calendar year. If at any time during the calendar year the time or place of
regular meetings, or of any regular meeting, is changed on a permanent or
temporary basis, a statement of the time and place of such changed regular
meetings shall be so posted by the Clerk at least twenty-four hours before the
time of the first changed regular meeting.
   (b)   The Clerk shall post a statement of the time and place of any
organizational meeting of Council at least twenty-four hours before the time of
such organizational meeting.
   (c)   Upon the adjournment of any regular or special meeting to another day,
the Clerk shall promptly post notice of the time and place of such adjourned
meeting.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)
107.05 NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETINGS.
   (a)   Except in the case of a special meeting referred to in Section
107.06(d), the Clerk shall, no later than twenty-four hours before the time of
a special meeting of Council, post a statement of the time, place and purposes
of such special meeting.
   (b)   The statement tendered under this section and the notifications under
Section
107.06 shall state such specific or general purpose or purposes then known to
the Clerk to be intended to be considered at such special meeting and may
state, as an additional general purpose, that any other business as may
properly come before Council at such meeting may be considered and acted upon.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)
107.06 NOTICE TO NEWS MEDIA OF SPECIAL MEETINGS.
   (a)   Any news medium organization that desires to be given advance
notification of special meetings of Council shall file with the Clerk a written
request therefor. Except in the event of an emergency requiring immediate
official action as referred to in subsection (d) hereof, a special meeting
shall not be held unless at least twenty-four hours advance notice of the time,
place and purposes of such special meeting is given to the news media that have
requested such advance notification in accordance with subsection (b) hereof.
   (b)   News media requests for advance notification of special meetings shall
specify:
      (1)   The name of the medium;
      (2)   The name and address of the person to whom written notifications to
the medium may be mailed, telegraphed or delivered;
      (3)   The names, addresses and telephone numbers, including addresses and
telephone numbers at which notifications may be given either during or outside
of business hours, of at least two persons to either one of whom oral
notifications to the medium may be given; and
      (4)   At least one telephone number which the request identifies as being
manned, and which can be called at any hour for the purpose of giving oral
notification to the medium.
   Any such request shall be effective for one year from the date of filing
with the Clerk or until the Clerk receives written notice from the medium
canceling or modifying the request, whichever is earlier. Each requesting news
medium shall be informed of the period of effectiveness at the time it files
its request. Such requests may be modified or extended only by filing a
complete new request with the Clerk. A request shall not be deemed to be made
unless it is complete in all respects, and such request may be conclusively
relied on by the City and the Clerk.
   (c)   The Clerk shall give such oral notification or written notification,
or both, as the Clerk determines, to the news media that have requested the
advance notification in accordance with subsection (b) hereof, of the time,
place and purposes of each special meeting, at least twenty-four hours prior to
the time of the special meeting.
   (d)   In the event of an emergency requiring immediate official action, a
special meeting may be held without giving twenty-four hours advance
notification thereof to the requesting news media. The persons calling such
meeting, or any one or more of such persons or the Clerk on their behalf, shall
immediately give oral notification or written notification, or both, as the
person or persons giving the notification determine, of the time, place and
purposes of the special meeting to the news media that have requested the
advance notification in accordance with subsection (b) hereof. The statement or
the call, or both, of any such special meeting shall state the general nature
of the emergency requiring immediate official action.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)
107.07 NOTIFICATION OF DISCUSSION OF SPECIFIC TYPES OF PUBLIC BUSINESS.
   (a)   Any person, upon written request and as provided herein, may obtain
reasonable advance notification of all meetings at which any specific type of
public business is scheduled to be discussed. Such person may file a written
request with the Clerk specifying:
      (1)   The person's name, and the address(es) and telephone number(s) at
or through which the person can be reached during and outside of business
hours;
      (2)   The specific type of public business the discussion of which the
person is requesting advance notification; and
      (3)   The number of calendar months, not to exceed twelve, which the
request covers.
   Such request may be canceled by request from such person to the Clerk. Each
such written request shall be accompanied by stamped, self-addressed envelopes
sufficient in number to cover the number of regular meetings during the time
period covered by the request and an estimated number of special meetings. The
Clerk shall notify, in writing, the requesting person when the supply of
envelopes is running out, and if the person desires notification after the
supply has run out, such person must deliver, to the Clerk, an additional
reasonable number of stamped, self-addressed envelopes as a condition to
receiving further notifications.
   The Clerk shall provide a standard form to be used for such requests. The
form shall set forth general subject matter categories to be checked off by the
requesting person.
   The requests may be modified or extended only by filing a complete new
request with the Clerk. A request shall not be deemed to be made unless it is
complete in all respects, and such request may be conclusively relied on by the
City and the Clerk.
   (b)   The Clerk shall give such advance notification under this section by
written notification, or by oral notification, or both, as the Clerk
determines.
   The contents of written notification under this subsection may be a copy of
the agenda of the meeting. Written notification under this subsection may be
accomplished by giving advance written notification, by copies of the agendas,
of all meetings of Council that are the subject of the request.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)
107.08 GENERAL PROVISIONS.
   (a)   Any person may visit or telephone the office of the Clerk during that
office's regular office hours to determine, based on information available at
that office:
      (1)   The time and place of regular meetings;
      (2)   The time, place and purposes of any then known special meetings;
and
      (3)   Whether the available agenda of any such future meeting states that
any specific type of public business, identified by the person, is to be
discussed at such meeting.
   (b)   Any notification provided herein to be given by the Clerk may be given
by any person acting in behalf of or under the authority of the Clerk.
   (c)   A reasonable attempt at notification shall constitute notification in
compliance with these rules.
(Ord. 7-76. Passed 2-2-76.)

shall be filed with the Director of Finance and the Clerk of Council and a copy
thereof shall be available for public inspection during normal business hours
in the Recreation Department office, City Hall Annex.
   (c)   All fees charged pursuant to subsection (a) hereof shall be credited
to the General Fund except fees of a deposit nature, which shall be credited to
the Recreation Trust Fund.
(Ord. 34-75. Passed 7-7-75.)

137.02 FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS SERVING AS CITY UTILITY BILL COLLECTION AGENTS.
   (a)   Agents for the collection of utility accounts, for the territory in
which the various utilities of the City serve customers, are hereby created and
established. Such agents shall furnish at their own expense suitable quarters,
and they shall be and are hereby authorized and directed to collect and receipt
utility bills of such City utility customers as may desire to take advantage
thereof. Such agents shall account for all moneys received at such intervals
and when called upon to do so by the Director of Finance, or by his duly
authorized representative. The collection records of the agents shall be open
to inspection by the Director of Finance, the Cashier/Office Manager of the
Utilities Office Division, and any duly authorized representative of either of
them, at all reasonable times.
   (b)   Such agents shall forward to the Cashier/Office Manager any and all
moneys collected and held, together with the stubs representing payments
received, at such intervals as is determined by the Director of Finance.
   (c)   Such agents, which shall be named by the City Manager, shall include
all financial institutions serving City utility customers, wherever located,
which desire to provide this service. Agents shall receive as compensation for
making such collections, a sum equivalent to six cents ($.06) for each utility
bill represented by a City utility bill stub. The aggregate sum to be paid each
agent for such service shall be paid monthly, which compensation is so allowed
for the reason that the amount of work involved in such collections and the
responsibility incurred warrants and justifies compensation for the service so
rendered.
   (d)   The Director of Finance is hereby authorized to prepare and adopt
rules and regulations by which agents shall be guided in the execution of this
service for the Utilities Office Division, Department of Finance, covering such
matters as no partial payments, no collection without customer bills, no
adjustments or alterations in utility bills, no acceptance of checks except
upon the responsibility of the collector, and such administrative matters.
(Ord. 15-81. Passed 4-6-81.)
137.03 PETTY CASH FUND, UTILITIES OFFICE DIVISION.
   In order to enable the cashier/office manager of the Utilities Office
Division of the Department of Finance to make daily deposits of the total daily
collections in the Electric, Water and Sewer Revenue Funds, there is hereby
established a petty cash fund in the Utilities Office Division. The petty cash
fund shall be in the amount of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00) and shall
be apportioned among the several funds as follows:
   (a)   $300.00 in the Electric Revenue Fund.
   (b)   225.00 in the Water Revenue Fund.
   (c)   225.00 in the Sewer Revenue Fund.
      $750.00 Total Utilities Office Division
(Ord. 5-99. Passed 4-19-99.)

137.06 CUSTODY AND DEPOSIT OF PUBLIC FUNDS.
   (a)   The Director of Finance shall have custody of all public funds
belonging to or under the control of the City, or any office, department or
agency of City government and shall deposit such funds in such active
depositories as may be designated by resolution of Council. Such designation
shall be made for a period of five years, beginning July 1, 2000 and continuing
every five years thereafter, or anytime during a designation period if it
determines that it is necessary and in the subdivision’s best interests to do
so.
   All public funds or moneys of the City not deposited in active depositories
shall be invested pursuant to the applicable provisions of Sections
137.07 through
137.31. As a result, interim and inactive depository agreements are
specifically not authorized.
   (b)   When a check from a customer or a direct debit authorized by a
customer is returned from the bank as a result of insufficient funds or the
bank account is closed, the customer will be assessed a fee that is sufficient
to cover the additional costs incurred by the City for processing the Returned
Bank Item unless the customer is able to show that the bank was in error. The
Director of Finance is authorized to establish the amount of such fee.
   (c)   The Director of Finance is hereby authorized and directed to prepare
and distribute a request for proposal for active depositories and other banking
services as may be required, in such form as he may devise, which form shall be
approved by the Director of Law. Such request shall serve as the basis for the
resolution of Council authorizing such active depositories. Each request for
proposal shall include a certified copy of this section, or as it may hereafter
be amended.
(Ord. 28-03. Passed 12-22-03.)
137.07 CUSTODY OF CITY INVESTMENTS AND INVESTED FUNDS.
   The Director of Finance shall have custody of all investments and invested
funds of the City, government, or in possession of such government in a
fiduciary capacity.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.08 CITY TREASURY INVESTMENT BOARD.
   The City Manager, the Director of Finance and the Director of Law shall
constitute the City Treasury Investment Board. The Director of Finance shall
serve as Secretary of the Board.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.09 INVESTMENT OF CITY MONEYS; POOLED FUNDS.
   Whenever there are moneys in the treasury of the City which will not be
required to be used by the City for current operating purposes, such moneys, in
lieu of being deposited in active depositories at a bank or banks, may be
invested by the Director of Finance, after consultation with the City Manager
and the Director of Law, meeting as the City Treasury Investment Board. The
Director of Finance is authorized to pool cash balances from the several funds
of the City for investment purposes.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.10 APPORTIONMENT OF INTEREST.
   (a)   All interest earned on moneys deposited in a bank(s) or invested in
accordance with the provisions of Section
137.09 shall, except as otherwise expressly provided by law, be credited to the
General Fund.
   (b)   Utility deposits held by the City in accordance with the applicable
provisions of the Codified Ordinances, and credited to the appropriate utility
deposit fund, shall be deposited in active accounts at a bank(s) or invested in
accordance with the provisions of Section
137.09.
   (c)   Interest earned on money invested in a utility deposit fund shall be
credited to that respective fund.
(Ord. 26-94. Passed 9-6-94.)
137.11 STATEMENT OF MONEYS.
   Whenever the money in the treasury of the City is to be invested as provided
for in Section
137.09, the Director of Finance shall submit to the City Manager and to the
Director of Law, a statement of moneys in the treasury or in the process of
collection, and a schedule showing the probable requirements of money for
current operating purposes, together with a recommendation as to whether any
moneys in the treasury shall be invested as provided therein. The City Manager
and the Director of Law concurring, the Director of Finance shall thereupon
order such investments of moneys in the treasury as may be most advisable in
the interest of the City. Whenever it is necessary to convert any such
investment into cash, such obligations shall be sold in any manner authorized
by law for the sale of investments, provided that no such obligations shall be
sold for less than their fair market value.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.12 RECORDS AND ACCOUNTS.
   The Director of Finance shall maintain an account to be known as the
Investment Account in which all transactions relating to the investment of such
treasury funds shall be entered. A record showing all bonds or other securities
purchased to be sold for the account of the treasury, with the number,
maturity, date and interest rate of each shall also be maintained. The Director
of Finance shall also keep a record of the number and maturity of interest
coupons, and whenever any such securities or interest coupons are due, shall
issue an order for their collection in the same manner as other receipts are
collected. Investments from pooled fund cash balances shall be recorded in this
account.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.13 CUSTODY OF SECURITIES.
   All securities belonging to the treasury of the City or to any fund thereof,
shall be in the custody of the Director of Finance, and shall be kept in a safe
deposit box or vault belonging to a regular City depository. Such safe deposit
box or vault shall be opened only in the presence of two of the three following
City officials, the Director of Finance, the Assistant Finance Director and the
Cashier/Office Manager, and only upon an order of the Director of Finance
directing the deposit or removal of securities purchased or sold, or the
clipping of interest coupons for collection. A report of whatever is placed in
or removed from such safe deposit box or vault upon any such occasion shall be
signed by the Director of Finance and by the witness or witnesses required by
this section, and shall be returned to the Director of Finance the same day.
Whenever any securities are so held for the City, the above officials shall
give bond to the City for the faithful performance of their duties as herein
provided. The bonds authorized by the Codified Ordinances shall meet this
requirement.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.14 OBJECTIVES AND GUIDELINES.
   The following investment and deposit objectives shall be applied in the
management of City funds:
   (a)   The primary objective of the City's investment activities is the
preservation of capital and the protection of investment principal.
   (b)   The City Treasury Investment Board shall strive to maximize the return
on the portfolio, but shall avoid assuming unreasonable investment risks.
   (c)   The City's investment portfolio shall remain sufficiently liquid to
enable the City to meet operating requirements which might reasonably be
anticipated.
   (d)   The City's investments shall be diversified to avoid the assumption of
unreasonable and avoidable risks associated with specific types of securities
or individual financial institutions.
   (e)    Investments shall be made with the exercise of that degree of
judgment and care, under circumstances then prevailing, which persons of
prudence, discretion and intelligence exercise in the management of their own
affairs, not for speculation but for investment, considering the probable
safety of their capital as well as the probable income to be derived.
   (f)   A factor in determining which depositories should hold the City's
public funds shall be the City's desire to obtain the best possible banking
services at the least possible cost.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.15 MATURITY OF INVESTMENTS.
   It is imperative that the City maintain sufficient liquidity to meet its
cash flow requirements. All investments shall be reviewed on an annual basis to
insure sufficient liquidity for the year.
(Ord. 14-93. Passed 6-7-93.)
137.16 AUTHORIZED FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND DEALERS.
   Securities shall be purchased only through financial institutions located
within the State of Ohio or through "primary securities dealers" as designated
by the Federal Reserve Bank. A list of these institutions shall be maintained
by the Director of Finance. The Director of Finance:
   (a)   May make additions to the authorized list when the investment and
deposit policy requirements are met;
   (b)   Shall make deletions from the list:
      (1)   If and as directed by ordinance of Council;
      (2)   Upon failure of the financial institution to meet the foregoing
investment and deposit policy requirements; or
      (3)   Upon request of the financial institutions or dealer; and
   (c)   May make deletions from the list if he determines that:
      (1)   The financial institution or dealer is experiencing financial
difficulties;
      (2)   There is consistent lack of competitiveness by the financial
institution or dealer;
      (3)   The account representative handling the City's account lacks
experience or familiarity in providing service to large institutional accounts;
or
      (4)   It is in the best interest of the City.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.17 INVESTMENTS AUTHORIZED.
   The Director of Finance, after consultation with the City Manager and the
Director of Law, and with the review and recommendation of the Citizen
Investment Advisory Committee, may invest on behalf of and in the name of the
City in the following instruments at a price not exceeding their fair market
value:
   (a)   Government securities, including:
      (1)   Negotiable direct obligations of the United States or obligations
issued by Federal agencies the principal of and interest on which are
unconditionally guaranteed by the United States, and bonds, notes, debentures
or other obligations or securities issued by any Federal Government agency,
whether or not they are guaranteed by the United States, including, but not
limited to, the following:
         A.   Direct obligations:
            1.   Treasury bills,
            2.   Treasury notes or bonds,
         B.   Obligations of the following Federal agencies:
            1.   Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA),
            2.   Small Business Association (SBA),
            3.   Federal Housing Administration (FHA),
            4.   Farmers Home Administration (FmHA),
            5.   General Services Administration (GSA).
      (2)   Obligations of the Federal Farm Credit Banks, Export-Import Bank of
Washington, Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, or Federal Home Loan Bank
or its district banks, including Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation
participation certificates, or obligations guaranteed by the Government
National Mortgage Association.
      (3)   Bonds of the State of Ohio and securities of the City.
   (b)   Nonnegotiable interest-bearing time certificates of deposits and
savings accounts in banks organized under the laws of this State, national
banks organized under the laws of the United States doing business and situated
in this State, savings and loan associations under State supervision, or
savings and loan associations located in this State and organized under Federal
law and under Federal supervision, provided that any such deposits and savings
accounts are secured by collateral as provided in Section
137.18.
   (c)   Repurchase agreements of a bank or savings and loan association
organized under the laws of the United States or any State thereof for
negotiable direct obligations of the United States, Federal agencies and
Federal instrumentalities as follows:
      (1)   U.S. Treasury bills, notes and bonds,
      (2)   Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA),
      (3)   Federal Farm Credit Bank obligations,
      (4)   Federal Home Loan Bank obligations.
   (d)   The State Treasury Asset Reserve of Ohio (Star Ohio), a statewide
investment pool managed by the Treasurer of the State of Ohio.
   (e)   Now Accounts, Super Now Accounts or any other similar account
authorized by the Federal Reserve's Depository Institutions' Deregulation
Committee.
(Ord. 20-94. Passed 7-18-94.)
137.18 SECURED BY PLEDGED COLLATERAL.
   All City funds deposited pursuant to Section
137.17(b) and (d) shall be secured by collateral pledged at market value in an
amount equal to at least one hundred percent (100%) of the deposit less the
amount incurred by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or the Federal
Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation. The following securities shall be
eligible to be pledged as collateral:
   (a)   Bonds, notes or other obligations of the United States; or bonds,
notes or other obligations guaranteed as to principal and interest by the
United States or those for which the faith of the United States is pledged for
the payment of principal and interest thereon, by language appearing in the
instruments specifically providing such guarantee or pledge and not merely by
interpretation or otherwise;
   (b)   Bonds, notes, debentures or other obligations or securities issued by
any Federal government agency, or the Export-Import Bank of Washington, bonds,
notes or other obligations guaranteed as to principal and interest by the
United States or those for which the faith of the United States is pledged for
the payment of principal and interest thereon, by interpretation or otherwise
and not by language appearing in the instruments specifically providing such
guarantee or pledge;
   (c)   Bonds and other obligations of this State;
   (d)   Bonds and other obligations of any county, township, school district,
municipal corporation, or other legally constituted taxing subdivision of this
State, which is not at the time of such deposit in default in the payment of
principal or interest on any of its bonds or other obligations for which the
full faith and credit of the issuing subdivision is pledged; and
   (e)   Bonds of other states of the United States which have not during the
ten years immediately preceding the time of such deposit defaulted in payments
of either interest or principal on any of their bonds.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.19 DELIVERY OF PLEDGED SECURITIES.
   Any securities pledged as collateral pursuant to Section
137.18 shall be delivered either to the Director of Finance or to an
independent financial institution approved by the Director of Finance to serve
as trustee (herein referred to as the "Trustee") under a trust agreement
therefor entered into between the City and such institution in a form approved
by the Director of Law. Fees and expenses of the Trustee shall be paid by the
depository.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.20 FAILURE TO PAY DEPOSIT.
   If the depository fails to pay over any part of a deposit due the City, the
Director of Finance shall have the option of selling in the manner determined
by the Director of Finance any of the securities deposited pursuant to the
provisions of this chapter. If the bonds or other securities are on deposit
with the Trustee, the Director of Finance may request the Trustee to deliver to
the Director of Finance any of the securities so deposited and the Director of
Finance shall have the option to sell such securities in the manner determined
by the Director of Finance. When a sale of securities has been made, upon
payment to the Director of Finance of the purchase money, the Director of
Finance shall transfer such securities to the purchaser whereupon the absolute
ownership of such securities shall pass to the purchaser. Any surplus remaining
after deducting the amount due the City and expenses of the sale shall be paid
to the depository.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.21 SUBSTITUTION OF PLEDGED SECURITIES.
   When a depository has deposited securities with the Trustee in accordance
with Section
137.19, the depository may substitute or exchange eligible securities having a
current market value equal to or greater than the current market value of the
securities then on deposit and for which they are to be substituted or
exchanged only:
   (a)   If the Director of Finance gives written authorization for such
substitution or exchange.
   (b)   If the Director of Finance has authorized the depository to make such
substitution or exchange on a continuing basis during a specified period
without prior approval of each substitution or exchange. Written authorization
shall be sent to the Trustee stating that substitution may be made on a
continuing basis during a specified period under the conditions specified
therein; or
   (c)   If no continuing authorization for substitution or exchange has been
given by the Director of Finance, the depository shall notify the Director of
Finance and the Trustee of an intended substitution or exchange, and the
Director of Finance fails to object to the Trustee within ten business days
after receipt by the Director of Finance of the notice of proposed
substitution. The notice to the Director of Finance and to the Trustee shall be
given in writing and delivered personally or by certified or registered mail
with a return receipt requested.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.22 NOTIFICATION OF SUBSTITUTION.
   The depository shall notify the Director of Finance of any substitution or
exchange of securities authorized pursuant to Section
137.21. Upon request from the Director of Finance, the depository and the
Trustee shall each furnish a detailed statement setting forth the face and
market values of all securities pledged.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
   137.23 POOLING OF PLEDGED SECURITIES.
   With the approval of the Director of Finance, a depository may provide
collateral for City funds deposited pursuant to Section
137.17 (b), (c) and (e) through a single pool of securities pledged for
deposits of all public funds held by the depository, subject to the following
conditions:
   (a)   Securities committed to the pool must have a market value at least
equal to one hundred ten percent (110%) of all public moneys on deposit with
the depository including the amount covered by Federal deposit insurance.
   (b)   The securities eligible for deposit in the pool shall be those
described in Section
137.18.
   (c)   The securities constituting the pool shall be delivered to a trustee
as described in Section
137.19. Fees and expenses of the trustee shall be paid by the depository.
   (d)   If the depository fails to pay over any part of the deposits due the
City, the Director of Finance may request the Trustee to deliver to the
Director of Finance any of the securities on deposit with the Trustee, provided
the value of the securities delivered shall not exceed the amount necessary to
produce an amount equal to City deposits made and not paid over, less the
portions of such deposits covered by Federal deposit insurance, plus any
accrued interest due on the deposits; in any event, the value of such
securities shall not exceed the City's proportional interest in the market
value of the pool as of the date of the depository's failure to pay over the
deposits. The Director of Finance shall have the option to sell the securities
in such manner as determined by the Director of Finance. Any surplus remaining
after deducting the amount due the City and expenses of the sale shall be paid
to the depository.
   (e)   Within thirty days of the end of each calendar quarter, the Trustee
shall provide a detailed statement setting forth the face and market value of
all securities pledged to the pool and the total of all public funds on
deposit.
   (f)   If at any time the market value of the pool is less than one hundred
ten percent (110%) of all public deposits held by the Trustee, the depository
shall immediately add securities to the pool sufficient to bring the market
value of the pool to at least one hundred ten percent ( 110%) of all public
funds on deposit with the Trustee.
   (g)    Failure of the institution to abide by any of the provisions of this
section shall be cause for the immediate suspension of the institution as a
qualified depository for any City funds.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.24 YIELD OF INVESTMENTS.
   The Director of Finance is hereby authorized and directed to invest the
City's funds so as to yield the highest returns consistent with the City
investment principles provided in Section
137.14 and applicable investment strategy.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.25 PRICE AND RATE QUOTATIONS.
   Price and rate quotations for all investments may be obtained from sources
within or outside the City. In the case of the sale or purchase of securities
where all other factors considered by the Director of Finance are equal,
placement shall be made in a banking institution situated within the City.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.26 BIDDING FOR INVESTMENTS.
   The Director of Finance is authorized and directed to seek competition in
the investment of all City funds and may invest all or part of such funds
outside the designated depository banks, provided the depository banks may bid
for such investments as any other financial institution.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.27 MONTHLY REPORTS.
   The Director of Finance is directed to provide monthly reports of the City's
investments to the City Manager and Council. (Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.28 TREASURY INVESTMENT BOARD NOT LIABLE FOR LOSS.
   The Director of Finance, the City Manager and the Director of Law, serving
as the City Treasury Investment Board, shall be relieved from any liability for
the loss of any public moneys deposited or invested pursuant to and in
compliance with this chapter, including, but not limited to, losses occasioned
by the sale of any instruments, securities or obligations, the closing of any
deposit accounts or the failure of any depository.
(Ord. 13-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.29 REQUEST TO PARTICIPATE IN STATE CONTRACTS.
   The City Manager hereby requests authority in the name of the City to
participate in State contracts which the Department of Administrative Services,
Office of State Purchasing has entered into for the purchase of supplies,
services, equipment and certain materials pursuant to Ohio R.C. 125.04.
(Ord. 14-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.30 AUTHORITY TO EXECUTE AGREEMENT.
   The City Manager is hereby authorized to agree in the name of the City to be
bound by all contract terms and conditions as the Department of Administrative
Services, Office of State Purchasing prescribes as a result of City
participation. Such terms and conditions may include a reasonable fee to cover
the administrative costs which the Department of Administrative Services incurs
as a result of participation in a contract. Further, the City Manager does
hereby agree to be bound by all such terms and conditions. (Ord. 14-86. Passed
6-2-86.)
137.31 AGREEMENT TO PAY VENDORS DIRECTLY.
   The City Manager is hereby authorized to agree in the name of the City to
pay directly the vendor, under each such State contract in which it
participates, for items it receives pursuant to the contract, and the City does
hereby agree to pay the vendor directly.
(Ord. 14-86. Passed 6-2-86.)
137.32 LINKED DEPOSIT PROGRAM.
   A "Linked Deposit Program" (Program) as defined in Ohio R.C. 135.80 is
established and the City Finance Director is authorized to place City
certificates of deposit at up to three percent (3.00%) below market rate with
an eligible lending institution applying for interim monies as provided in Ohio
R.C. 135.08 or inactive money as provided in Ohio R.C. 135.32 provided the
institution agrees to lend the value of such deposit to eligible borrowers at
up to three percent (3.00%) below the present borrowing rate applicable to each
borrower pursuant to the provisions as set forth herein.
   (a)   To be eligible for participation in the City’s Linked Deposit Program,
a borrower shall comply with the following:
      (1)   Locate and maintain within the City, any and all business
operations benefiting from participation in the City’s Linked Deposit Program.
      (2)   Conduct all benefiting business operations in compliance with
applicable federal, state and local laws.
      (3)   Prohibit discrimination against any employee or applicant for
employment because of race, color, religion, sex, age, handicap or national
origin; and
      (4)   Timely prepare and deliver to the City such written reports as may
be, from time to time, requested by the City to monitor the effectiveness of
the City’s Linked Deposit Program.
   (b)   The application and application review procedures for a borrower’s
participation in the City’s Linked Deposit Program shall be as follows:
      (1)   The borrower must apply to a participating banking institution for
program participation;
      (2)   The borrower must be approved for participation by the banking
institution pursuant to said institution’s standard loan approval criteria;
      (3)   If approved by the banking institution, the borrower’s application
shall be sent to the City Manager for approval;
      (4)   The City Manager shall forward the borrower’s application to the
City Economic Development Manager and the City Finance Director, acting as the
City Economic Development Team, for approval; and
      (5)   The City Economic Development Team shall review each application
and recommend to the City Manager, approval or disapproval of the application.
The City Economic Development Team shall consider the following when
determining whether approval shall be recommended:
         A.   Unpaid fines, orders, permit fees, taxes and City utility bills
owed by applicant;
         B.   The goals and objectives of the Program;
         C.   Funds available in the Program;
         D.   Compliance with the Program’s participation requirements; and
         E.   Special circumstances identified with the borrower’s application.
      (6)   The Economic Development Team shall forward its recommendation for
application acceptance to the City Manager. Upon receipt of said
recommendation, the City Manager shall decide whether the application is to be
accepted, and shall immediately notify the banking institution of said
decision.
      (7)   Upon the banking institution’s receipt of notice from the City
Manager that the borrower’s application has been approved, the banking
institution shall complete the lending transaction pursuant to the provisions
of this Program and its own implementation criteria.
   (c)   To be eligible to participate in the City’s Linked Deposit Program, a
lending institution must first enter into an agreement with the City to carry
out the purposes of the Program pursuant to the terms as established by the
City.
   (d)   The City Finance Director shall annually provide to Council a detailed
report on the operation of the City’s Linked Deposit Program.
(Ord. 5-02. Passed 2-19-02.)
137.33   POLICY REGARDING AMENITIES FOR PARTICIPANTS AT MEETINGS AND OTHER
OCCASIONS.
   (a)   The City recognizes the value in providing meals, refreshments, and/or
other amenities for staff, council, citizens, advisory groups, who participate
in meetings and staff development sessions, or on other occasions as deemed
appropriate by the administration.
   (b)   Such amenities may include, but are not limited to, the examples
listed below and are less than fifty dollars ($50.00) per person. Items may
include employee recognition items, gifts appropriate to the occasion, an
employee or departmental picnic for staff, coffee mugs, food, caps, clothing,
educational items, books, or similar items of a reasonable value.
   (c)   The Administration hereby affirms that these expenses do serve a valid
and proper public purpose. The "public purpose" served is for the promotion of
the City, the promotion of education, enhancement of morale, and rapport, and
the encouragement of participation in said activities. Under no circumstances
shall public funds be expended for the purchase of alcoholic beverages.
   (d)   The Administration further directs the Director of Finance to include
funds in the annual appropriations for the purchase of such amenities or to
reimburse staff who incur such expenses if purchased in connection with
meetings, staff development sessions, or other occasions deemed appropriate by
the Administration. All such expenditures on behalf of the City must have prior
authorization by the City Manager and will be made in accordance with all City
purchasing procedures and the Ohio Ethic Laws. Documentation is required to be
provided.
(Res. 62-23. Passed 11-6-23.)
137.34 LIABILITY FOR LOSS OF PUBLIC FUNDS.
   The Treasurer, or other officer of the municipality having the duties of a
treasurer or of a city auditor, shall not be held liable for a loss of public
funds when the officer has performed all official duties required of the
officer with reasonable care, but shall be liable only when a loss of public
funds results from the officer's negligence or other wrongful act.
(R.C. § 733.82)

141.01 POLICE DIVISION AUTHORITY.
   The Police Division shall have the powers, duties and authority provided by
the Ohio Revised Code and shall be subject to control by the City Manager as
executive head.
(1967 Code Sec. 36.05)
141.02 ELIGIBILITY FOR EMPLOYMENT .
   No person shall be eligible to receive an original appointment as a
policeman or policewoman in an open competitive examination unless he or she
has reached the age of twenty- one and has not attained the age of thirty-
seven. In the case of an appointment for a lateral transfer person who is
subject to a lateral civil service examination, no person shall be eligible to
receive an appointment as a policeman or policewoman unless he or she has
reached the age of twenty-one and has not attained the age of thirty-five
provided they have at least one year of full time law enforcement experience:
or has not attained the age of forty-one provided that they have at least three
years full time law enforcement experience, or has not attained the age of
forty-nine provided they have at least five years of full time law enforcement
experience.
(Ord. 14-71. Passed 3-29-71; Ord. 2-20. Passed 2-3-20; Ord. 08-23. Passed 4-3-
23.)
141.03 SERVICE TO OTHER MUNlClPALITIES.
   (a)   Pursuant to Ohio R.C. 737.041, Council hereby authorizes the City
Manager, the Chief of the Police Division and the officers on duty in charge of
the Police Division to render the services of the Police Division to other
municipalities, townships, counties or the State in times of emergency, whether
or not the City has entered into mutual aid contracts for police services with
any of those political subdivisions or the State. The determination of "times
of emergency" shall be made only by the City Manager, the Chief of the Police
Division or the officers on duty in charge of the Police Division upon a call
for emergency police protection services by the State or another political
subdivision of this State.
   (b)   The personnel of the Police Division rendering emergency services to
other political subdivisions shall, as provided by State law, be entitled to
all of their usual wages and benefits, shall be covered by Workers'
Compensation and shall be immune from any liability arising from the reasonable
good faith rendered of emergency police protection services.
(Ord. 28-89. Passed 7-17-89.)
141.04 PARKING ENFORCEMENT UNIT.
   (a)   Appointment of Members.  There is created within the City Police
Division a Parking Enforcement Unit, the members of which shall be appointed by
the City Manager.
   (b)   Term of Service.  Parking enforcement officers shall serve so long as
the City Manager may direct, or until a resignation submitted by any such
member is accepted by the Director of Public Safety.
   (c)   Qualification of Members. The members of the Unit may not be under the
age of twenty-one years at the time of their appointment, and such other
requirements as provided by rules adopted under subsection (e) hereof.
   (d)   Control of Unit. The Chief of Police shall be the commanding officer
of the Unit, and shall have control of the assignment, training, stationing,
and the direction of work of such Unit. The Unit shall perform only such duties
as are assigned by the Chief of Police, and shall act only when in the
prescribed uniform or partial uniform. Such members shall obey the chain of
command of the Police Division and shall take orders from all regularly
appointed members thereof.
   (e)   Rules. The Director shall prescribe rules for the organization,
administration, conduct, and control of the Unit.
   (f)   Uniform. The Director is authorized to prescribe the type of uniform
or partial uniform to be worn by members of the unit. The Chief of Police shall
prescribe the times and places when the same shall be worn.
   (g)   Compensation. Parking Enforcement Unit members shall be paid at a rate
established by the City Manager/Director of Public Safety.
   (h)   Nonliability. This section is declared to be for the protection of
public peace, health, property, safety, and general welfare, and neither the
City nor any agent or representative of the City, any officer appointed under
this section, or any individual, firm, partnership, corporation, or the
receiver or trustees or any other agent thereof, who in good faith executes any
executive order or rule promulgated pursuant to this section shall be liable
for injury or damage sustained as the direct or proximate result of such
action.
(Ord. 24-95. Passed 10-16-95.)

143.03 EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICE RATES AND REGULATIONS.
   (a)   Every person using the services of the Division of Fire Emergency
Medical Service unit or guardian of such person or any other person who is
financially responsible for such person, shall be liable for the payment of the
charges that are established by this section.
   (b)   The City Manager is hereby authorized to establish rates and charges
in connection with the delivery of various levels of emergency medical services
by the Division of Fire and shall file such rates and charges with the Director
of Finance and the Clerk of Council on an annual basis.
   (c)   (1)   The City will provide transport and emergency medical service to
the non- resident user and the City will request full payment from the non-
resident user at the rate established by this section for the level of service
provided. The City shall bill the insurance company, if any, and/or the non-
resident for the service as required by this section.
      (2)   The City will provide transport and emergency medical service in
exchange for the assignment of insurance company proceeds available to the
resident user and the City shall only bill the resident and their insurers,
including the Federal Health Care program of Medicare and Medicaid, for the
services provided but only to the extent of their insurance coverage. The City
shall treat revenues received from local taxes as payment of any otherwise
applicable co-payments and deductibles that would otherwise be due to the City.
   (d)   The City Manager is authorized to enter into an agreement with a
company that will provide electronic claims filing system for the purpose of
collecting insurance proceeds identified in this section.
   (e)   The City Manager is hereby authorized to establish guidelines and
procedures to implement the fees and charges associated with the implementation
of this section.
(Ord. 40-02. Passed 12-16-02.)

five members who shall serve without compensation. Members shall be appointed

167.021 RESIDENCE REQUIREMENTS FOR DEPARTMENT HEADS, DIVISION HEADS AND SENIOR
SUPERVISORS. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section 167.021 was repealed in its entirety by Ordinance

167.03 DEFINITION AND ADOPTION OF THE CLASSIFICATION PLAN.
   (a)   Classification of Positions. All positions in the Municipal service
whose salaries/wages are determined by the legislative authority, except those
positions listed in Section
167.09, shall be grouped into classes and each class shall include those
positions sufficiently similar in respect to their duties and responsibilities
so that similar requirements as to training, experience, knowledge, skill,
personal qualities and the same rates of compensation are applicable thereto.
These positions, with the exceptions as above, shall be known as classified
positions of the City.
   (b)   Preparation and Content of Class Specifications. Class specifications
shall be prepared and maintained under the direction of the City Manager for
all classified positions and, when the positions of the class are under civil
service, shall be approved by the Civil Service Commission. These
specifications shall define the duties of all positions and the desirable
qualifications as set forth in the class specifications and it shall be
understood that all positions require: United States citizenship, ability to
read, write, speak and understand the English language and to follow written
and oral instructions, good physical condition; ability to get along with
others; sobriety, integrity, loyalty and a record of orderly, law-abiding
citizenship; and, in positions involving the operation of a motor vehicle, a
vehicle operator’s license issued by the State of Ohio.
   (c)   Adoption of Classification Plan. The classes of positions as set forth
in Section
167.07, and the specifications for the respective classes, are hereby adopted
and shall constitute the classification plan on the basis of which such
positions shall be classified. Those classes of positions which are subject to
the provisions of civil service in accordance with the statutes, City
ordinances and the rules and regulations of the Civil Service Commission are
designated by an asterick (*) preceding the class titles in Section
167.07.
(Ord. 39-89. Passed 10-2-89.)
167.04 APPLICATION AND INTERPRETATION OF CLASSIFICATION PLAN.
   (a)   Allocation of Existing Positions. The classified positions are hereby
allocated to appropriate classes in accordance with the schedules attached
hereto. Each employee shall be notified of the allocation of the position, and
each employee having served in any such position which is under civil service
for three months or more, is hereby given civil service status in such
position, subject to the approval and certification by the Civil Service
Commission of the employee’s qualification to serve in such position.
   (b)   Interpretation of Class Specifications.
      (1)   Purpose and effect of class specifications. Each class
specification outlines the main characteristics and qualification requirements
of positions in the class and gives examples of specific duties which employees
holding such positions may properly be required to perform. Each class
specification is descriptive and explanatory but not restrictive. The listing
of particular examples of duties does not preclude the assignment of other
tasks when considered necessary by the department head.
      (2)   Application of specifications to positions. In determining the
class to which a position should be allocated, the specifications of each class
shall be considered in its entirety and in relation to the specifications of
other classes in the classification plan.
      (3)   Statement of desirable qualifications. The statement of
qualifications in a class specification is intended to be used as a guide in
selecting candidates for employment, as an aid in the preparation of
competitive examinations, and for use in determining the relative value of
positions in the class with positions in other classes.
(Ord. 24-59. Passed 6-15-59.)
167.05 ADMINISTRATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION PLAN.
   (a)   The City Manager shall be responsible for the maintenance of the
classification and compensation plan, including, but not limited to the
allocation of new or changed positions; the determination of proper
compensation rates within the ordinance provisions; maintenance of up-to-date
class specifications, class lists and allocation records; and the preparation
of recommendations to Council and/or Civil Service Commission, on revisions to
the plan on the basis of changes in duties of positions and in prevailing rates
of pay for comparable occupations outside the City service. The City Manager
may delegate administrative and clerical work involved in the foregoing to any
appropriate employee or employees.
   (b)   Subject to Civil Service Commission approval where required, the City
Manager shall provide for the re-allocation of any position from one class to
another class whenever a change in duties and responsibilities of such position
makes the class to which the position was previously allocated no longer
applicable. Any proposed re-allocation shall be made with the knowledge of the
employee concerned and his department head.
   (c)   The approval of Council shall be obtained for the establishment of any
new class or any change in class. Such changes shall take the form of
amendments to this chapter. Approval of the Civil Service Commission shall be
required for any changes affecting positions under civil service.
   (d)   The biweekly and hourly rates for different classes of positions which
are prescribed in this chapter shall be changed only upon recommendation of the
City Manager and amendment of this chapter by Council. Changes of the
compensation plan shall be made in a manner to maintain proper percentage
relationships among the classes of positions and to reflect changes in
prevailing rates of pay for comparable positions outside the City service.
   (e)   Any employee shall have the right to consideration of any request he
may have with respect to the application of the classification and compensation
plan to his position. The employee shall initially make his request to the
department head who shall promptly seek to arrive at a solution which is
consistent with the plan and acceptable to the employee. Where the department
head is unable to resolve such a request in the manner that the employee is
willing to accept in writing, the matter shall be submitted to the City Manager
for a solution which is consistent with the plan and acceptable to the
employee.
(1967 Code Secs. 30.22, 30.58)

conditions for the members of that local.

incorporated into
Chapter 167 of the Codified Ordinances of the City of Painesville, as setting
forth the applicable rates of compensation, benefit provisions, and working
conditions for the members of that lodge.
   (c)   The collective bargaining agreement between the Fraternal Order of
Police, Ohio Labor Council, and Lodge No. 90 Sergeants and Lieutenants, and the
City of Painesville, effective April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2027, is hereby
adopted and incorporated into
Chapter 167 of the Codified Ordinances of the City of Painesville, as setting
forth the applicable rates of compensation, benefit provisions, and working
conditions for the members of that union.
   (d)   The collective bargaining agreement between the Fraternal Order of
Police, Ohio Labor Council, and Lodge No. 90 Community Service Officers and
School Resource Officers, and the City of Painesville, effective April 1, 2024
through March 31, 2027, is hereby adopted and incorporated into
Chapter 167 of the Codified Ordinances of the City of Painesville, as setting
forth the applicable rates of compensation, benefit provisions, and working
conditions for the members of that union.
   (e)   The collective bargaining agreement between the International Union of
Operating Engineers 18S and the City of Painesville, effective April 1, 2024
through March 31, 2027, is hereby adopted and incorporated into
Chapter 167 of the Codified Ordinances of the City of Painesville, as setting
forth the applicable rates of compensation, benefit provisions and working
conditions for the members of that union.
   (f)   The collective bargaining agreement between the International
Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and the City of Painesville, effective April

167 of the Codified Ordinances of the City of Painesville, as setting forth the
applicable rates of compensation, benefit provisions, and working conditions
for members of that union.
   (g)   The collective bargaining agreement between the American Federation of
State, County and Municipal Employees, Ohio Council 8 and the City of

and incorporated into

   (h)   The City Manager is authorized and directed to execute the above
collective bargaining agreements.

167.08 DEFINITION AND APPLICATION OF NORMAL WORK WEEK.
   (a)   The normal non-bargaining work week shall consist of seven consecutive
twenty-four hour periods during which an employee shall be assigned to any five
eight-hour work days. This applies to all full-time employees. This does not
under any circumstance guarantee the number of hours an employee may be
required to work, nor does it guarantee forty hours of work in each week. This
section is for definition purposes only.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XI,
Normal Work Week.
(Ord. 1-00. Passed 1-18-00.)

167.10 PAY RATES AND PERIODS.
   (a)   Designation of Pay Periods. All salaries, wages and compensation of
officers and employees, except as otherwise provided herein, shall be paid
biweekly. This includes all personnel of the Municipal Court. President of
Council and Council members shall be paid monthly.
   (b)   Compensation Schedules. The pay of City employees occupying positions
covered by this section shall be on the basis of appropriate schedules of
biweekly and hourly rates as prescribed in the designated compensation sections
for the respective classes of positions.
   For each salary and hourly wage grade, a pay range is hereby established
which shall consist of an entrance rate, four intermediate rates and a maximum
rate, comprising the base rates for the pay grade.
   The schedules of biweekly and hourly rates shown in the appropriate
compensation sections, together with the provisions on benefits and working
conditions shall comprise the Compensation Plan.
   For subsections (a) and (b) hereof, union employees, refer to your
Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XII, Compensation Plan.
   (c)   Full-Time Basis of Pay Rates. The biweekly pay rates for salary-rated
employees prescribed in the compensation schedules are based on full-time
employment at normal working hours for the respective classes of positions as
indicated in the classified positions section; provided however, that the
salaries of salary-rated department/division heads and senior supervisors
assigned to Class Grade 19 and above are fixed according to the
responsibilities to be fulfilled and are not based on a fixed number of hours
of work per week and shall not be adjusted with variation in work schedules,
unless part-time employment is specifically provided.
   All regular, full-time employees shall be paid the rates prescribed in the
appropriate compensation schedules for their respective classes of positions.
   Compensation of part-time positions shall be determined as provided in the
section designated for computation of salaries for part-time employees.
   Classes to be paid on an hourly basis are designated in the sections
provided for compensation for hourly-rated employees.
   In cases where a portion of the compensation is paid to an employee by
another governmental agency, such portion shall be deducted from the rates
prescribed for the purpose of computing the amount to be paid by the City.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
