167.14 PERCENTAGE LONGEVITY COMPENSATION PLAN.
   (a)   All employees who have ten years of continuous satisfactory service
with the City shall receive a two and one-half percent (2 1/2%) increase on
their rate if they have at least six months of satisfactory service.
   (b)   All employees who have fifteen years of continuous satisfactory
service with the City shall receive a five percent (5%) increase on their rate
if they have at least six months of satisfactory service.
   (c)   All employees who have twenty years of continuous satisfactory service
with the City shall receive a seven and one-half percent (7 1/2%) increase on
their rate if they have at least six months of satisfactory service.
   (d)   All employees who have twenty-five years of continuous satisfactory
service shall receive a ten percent (10%) increase on their rate if they have
at least six months of satisfactory service.
(Ord. 18-97. Passed 7-7-97.)
167.141 FLAT RATE LONGEVITY COMPENSATION PLAN.
   Effective April 1, 1997, all employees who are not receiving longevity
payments under the “Percentage Longevity” plan shall become eligible for
longevity payments pursuant to the below schedule, only. Any employee receiving
longevity payments under the “Percentage Longevity” plan on April 1, 1997,
shall continue to receive payments under such plan, instead of the new plan set
forth below.
   (a)   All employees who have ten years of service with the City shall
receive a one thousand five hundred twenty dollar ($1,520) increase if they
have at least six months of satisfactory service at the maximum rate in the pay
plan.
   (b)   All employees who have 15 years service with the City shall receive a
two thousand seventy dollar ($2,070) increase if they have at least six months
of satisfactory service.
   (c)   All employees who have 20 years service with the City shall receive a
two thousand six hundred twenty dollar ($2,620) increase if they have at least
six months of satisfactory service.
   (d)   All employees who have 25 years service with the City shall receive a
three thousand two hundred eighty dollar ($3,280) increase if they have at
least six months of satisfactory service.
   (e)   Employees shall be eligible to receive the annual longevity as
provided on their anniversary date. Employees may elect to have this longevity
payment put in a deferred compensation program to the extent permitted by law,
provided such employee notifies the City of such election at least 30 days
prior to her/his anniversary date.
   (f)   Effective February 19, 2025, employees, whether full, part or
permanent part time (i) who have retired from City service and then began to
collect a pension from the Ohio Public Employee Retirement System ("OPERS") or
the Ohio Police and Fire Pension System ("OP&F"); or (ii) who left the City
service for other reasons and then began to collect a pension from opers or
OP&F and who then became or become reemployed by the City while they are
receiving a pension from OPERS or OP&F are designated full, part or permanent
part time as a retire - rehire employee ("retire - rehire employee") and any
such retire - rehire employees are not eligible for longevity payments based on
their prior service with the City. Instead, a retire - rehire employee's
eligibility for longevity payments shall begin when they become reemployed with
the city and only their service time while re-employed shall be used to
calculate their eligibility for longevity pay based on the reemployed time
frames in the schedule above.
   For overtime purposes, the longevity payment shall be divided by 2,080 and
added to the employee’s base rate of pay.
(Ord. 15-02. Passed 6-17-02; Ord. 9-18. Passed 7-16-18; Ord. 2-19. Passed 1-22-
19; Ord. 08- 25. Passed 2-18-25.)
167.15 EMPLOYER PICK-UP PLAN.
   (a)   An Employer Pick-Up Plan is hereby established in accordance with the
requirements as set forth in Section 414(h)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code, in
which the City agrees to pick up all or a portion of the employee's
contribution to the Ohio Public Employees' Retirement System, and the Police
and Firemen's Pension Fund of Ohio as may be determined by ordinance of Council
for all eligible employees covered by this agreement, and to pay the amount
picked up to the plan as an employer contribution in lieu of contributions by
the employee. The Ohio Public Employees' Retirement System (OPERS) meets the
qualification requirements of Section 401(a) of the Internal Revenue Service
Code.
   (b)   All employees shall have their gross compensation, as established by
the appropriate compensation schedules, reduced by the full picked up amounts
as determined by OPERS, to arrive at an adjusted gross compensation amount for
Federal and State income tax purposes.
   (c)   Employee Eligibility. All full-time employees of the City are eligible
for and shall be included in the Employer Pick-Up Plan.
   (d)   Employees May Not Receive Contributions Directly. Eligible employees
shall not have the option of choosing to receive the contributed amounts
directly instead of having them paid by the City to the Public Employees
Retirement System.
   (e)   Service Credit Purchase. Employees may elect to use the pick-up
deduction to purchase additional service credit or redeposit contributions
previously withdrawn plus interest as permitted by Ohio R.C. Chapter 145 and in
conformance with the plan described in subsection (a) hereof. Employees who
elect to participate in this plan cannot increase, decrease or terminate the
amount of the pick-up deduction until it is paid in full.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06.)
167.151 PICK-UP PLAN RATE.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06.)
167.16 ENTRANCE COMPENSATION RATES.
   (a)   Starting Rate on Initial Employment. Original appointment to any
position shall be made at the entrance rate and advancement from the entrance
rate to the maximum rate within a compensation range shall be by successive
steps. Upon recommendation of the department head, the City Manager may approve
initial compensation at a rate higher than the minimum rate in the compensation
schedule for the class, when the needs of the service make such action
necessary; provided, that any such exception is based on the outstanding and
unusual character of the employee's pertinent experience and ability over and
above the minimum qualifications specified for the class.
   (b)   Starting Rate on Return to Duty. When an employee returns to duty in
the same class of position after separation from the City service of not more
than one year, which separation was not due to discreditable circumstances, the
employee shall receive the rate in the compensation schedule corresponding to
the step rate received at the time of separation and shall subsequently serve
thereat for at least such period as is normally required for advancement to the
next higher step rate.
   (c)   Rate of Compensation on Promotion. Unless otherwise specifically
authorized, in any case where an employee is promoted to a class with a higher
compensation schedule, the employee shall be paid on the basis of either
subsection (c)(1) or (2) hereof, whichever is higher:
      (1)   The entrance rate for the new position, or
      (2)   A rate in the grade for the new position which is equal to (or the
first rate higher than) the same step in the next higher grade above the
employee's former grade.
   Subsequent advancement within the compensation schedule shall be as
determined by the compensation schedule, and/or Sections
167.14 and
167.17.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XII,
Compensation Plan.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.161 RATE OF COMPENSATION ON RECLASSIFICATION AFTER IMPLEMENTATION OF 1985
CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION PLAN.  (Applies to individual employees only.)
   Unless otherwise specifically designated, in any case where an employee is
reclassified to a class with a higher compensation schedule, without a change
in class title or without a change in duties if the class title is changed, the
entrance rate shall be at the step in the higher schedule that will reflect the
years of service in the position, or in continuous service with the City as
existed immediately prior to the reclassification. Subsequent advancement
within the compensation schedule shall be as determined by the compensation
schedule and/or Sections
167.14 and
167.17.
(Ord. 25-85. Passed 8-19-85.)
167.162 EFFECTIVE DATE OF RATE ADJUSTMENT.
   Any adjustment in rate of compensation of any City employee occupying a
classified position shall become effective the first day of the pay period in
which the adjustment is granted.
(Ord. 20-91. Passed 8-19-91.)
167.163 RATE OF COMPENSATION ON RECLASSIFICATION AND/OR IMPLEMENTATION OF 1985
CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION PLAN. (Applies to all employees as a group.)
   The implementation and installation of the 1985 Classification and
Compensation Plan shall be as follows:
   (a)   Present rates that are below the minimum for the class to which a
position has been allocated, shall be increased to the minimum rate of the pay
grade.
   (b)   Present rates that are within a pay grade and coincide with a pay step
shall be retained at that step.
   (c)   Present rates that fall within a pay grade, but do not fall on a step,
shall be adjusted to the next higher step.
   (d)   Present rates that are at or above the maximum step of the pay grade,
including longevity, would not be changed as of the date of reclassification
and/or implementation of the pay plan. Such present rates shall remain in
effect until subsequent adjustments, changes or increases in the revised pay
plan, including longevity, result in increasing the rate for the pay grade to
an amount in excess of the present rate. At that time, the employee’s pay grade
would revert from the previous amount to the new rate.
   (e)   In the case of employees in grades 19 and above, except fire captains
and police lieutenants, rates would be reflected in Section
167.12. Within-grade increases thereafter would depend on individual
performance as determined by the City Manager and other top administrative
officials.
   (f)   Subsections (a) through (e) hereof, notwithstanding, present employees
who were employed or promoted under the former Classification and Compensation
Plan, and who are in Step 1 (or Entrance Rate) or Step 2 after six months in
their respective Class Grades, and new employees, hired during the period April
1, 1985 through May 20, 1985, shall continue to progress through these pay
steps in accordance with the time period and terms of employment as authorized
at their date of appointment. In the event that the application of this
provision or the provisions of subsections (a) through (e) hereof result in an
employee’s being reclassified to a step higher than under the former
compensation plan during the first twelve months of employment or promotion,
such step increase shall be considered as an "advance step-up", and this step
and rate shall be continued at the date of the next scheduled step increase
that would have occurred under the former plan, "normal step-up". An employee
shall not advance to a higher step, at the completion of the first twelve
months of employment or promotion, under the 1985 Classification and
Compensation Plan than they would have been eligible under the former plan.
Subsequent advancement within the compensation schedule shall be as determined
by the compensation schedule and/or Sections
167.14 and
167.17.
(Ord. 25-85. Passed 8-19-85.)
167.17 PROBATION AND ADVANCEMENT WITHIN THE COMPENSATION RANGE.
   (a)   After initial appointment or promotion to a position, the first 12
months of service shall be considered a probationary period, which may be
extended. In the event of a promotion, the employee shall be reviewed each six
months for performance so as to keep the employee abreast of his or her
progress in the new position. Upon the satisfactory conclusion of the probation
period, the compensation of the employee may be advanced to the next higher
step in the grade for the class in which the employee's position is allocated.
Such employee shall subsequently serve thereat for at least such period as is
normally required for advancement to the next higher step rate. An increase in
class grade without a change in class title shall not constitute a promotion
within the meaning of this section. In the event that the employee does not
satisfactorily complete the probation period, he or she shall be terminated
from employment.
   (b)   Should an employee within a position requiring specific licensure
within a specific time frame be unable to obtain such licensure, the employee
shall be terminated.
   (c)   Union Employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06.)
167.18 RECOMMENDATIONS FOR ADVANCEMENT WITHIN A COMPENSATION SCHEDULE.
   The department head concerned shall recommend in writing to the City Manager
the advancement in rate of each employee in his department who, in his opinion,
has met the requirements for compensation advancement as enumerated above. In
the case of advancement upon completion of the probationary period, the
recommendation shall include the certification that the probation period has
been successfully completed. In the case of subsequent advancements within a
schedule, the recommendation shall include a certification that the employee’s
service has been entirely satisfactory for at least three months immediately
prior to the effective date of the recommended advancement in rate of pay.
(1967 Code Sec. 30.28)
167.19 COMPUTATION OF SALARIES OF PART-TIME EMPLOYEES.
   (a)   Any salaried employee regularly employed on a continuous work schedule
of less than full-time shall be compensated at an adjusted rate of pay.
   (b)   A part-time or seasonal employee occupying a classified position may
be advanced in pay based upon meritorious service in the same manner as other
employees, except that only actual time worked shall be considered in the
computation of service requirements for such advancement. When the service time
equivalent of required periods of service has been attained, advancement to the
higher step rates may be effected in accordance with Section
167.17. The accumulation of service toward advancement with a class shall
continue unless interrupted by a period of absence from the City for more than
one year or by absence without leave as provided in Section
167.24.
(Ord. 12-93. Passed 5-17-93.)
167.20 PLUS RATES FOR HIGHER SKILLS AND/OR SUPERVISION.
   (a)   In any case where an employee is qualified for and required to serve
in a supervisory capacity, or to accept the responsibilities for work in a
higher classification and/or position and if such employee performs these
services for four or more continuous hours, such employee shall be paid an
additional five percent (5%) of their base rate, rather than moving to the
higher grade.
   Provided, however, the above provisions shall not apply if the class
specifications specifically provide that it is part of the employee’s normal
duties to assume the responsibilities of the higher classification position in
the absence of the employee holding the position.
   (b)   When an employee is required to work overtime, either in a supervisory
capacity and/or for work in a higher classification, such overtime shall be
paid at the higher rate for each hour(s) or portions thereof worked in that
capacity.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XII,
Compensation Plan.
(Ord. 9-95. Passed 6-5-95; Ord. 28-21. Passed 11-1-21.)
167.21 PLUS RATES FOR SUPERVISING EMPLOYEES IN THE SAME CLASS GRADE.
   In the event the employee is required to be in charge of one or more
employees in positions of the same classification, such employee shall be paid
at the same step in the next higher grade, provided, however, the assignment is
for a period of four or more continuous hours.
   An employee may be temporarily assigned to work at any position in the same
or lower class grade without change in pay.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XII,
Compensation Plan.
(Ord. 12-93. Passed 5-17-93.)
167.22 PLANT OPERATORS' RATES.
(EDITOR'S NOTE: Former Section 167.22 was repealed by Ordinance 12-93, passed
May 17, 1993.)
167.23 SHIFT DIFFERENTIAL.
   A shift differential shall be paid to hourly rated employees and salary
rated shift supervisors at the Electric Generation, Water Pollution Control,
and Water Purification Plants working in jobs regularly assigned as second and
third shift operations. The second shift differential shall consist of sixty-
five cents (65¢) per hour for hours actually worked during the regularly
scheduled second shift. The third shift differential shall consist of eighty
cents (80¢) per hour for hours actually worked during the regularly scheduled
third shift.
   Shift differential shall not be paid on "doubleback" situations.
   The shift differential in effect at the start of the regularly scheduled
shift shall continue to be the differential paid as the result of overtime
worked into another shift differential eligible shift.
   Shift differential shall not be paid on hours compensated (either worked or
not worked) during an emergency call-out.
(Ord. 15-02. Passed 6-17-02.)
167.24 REQUIREMENTS AS TO CONTINUITY OF SERVICE.
   Service requirements for advancement within compensation schedules and for
other purposes as specified in this chapter shall have the implication of
continuous service, which means employment in the City service without a break
or interruption. Leave of absence with or without pay of not to exceed thirty-
one consecutive days shall not interrupt continuous service nor be deducted
therefrom. Leave of absence without pay in excess of thirty-one days, except
for extended service with the Armed Forces of the United States, shall be
deducted in computing total service, but shall not serve to interrupt
continuous service.
   All absences without leave in excess of one day shall be deducted from, and
all absences without leave in excess of three days shall interrupt continuity
of service. In case of repeated absences without leave, the City Manager may
consider the service of the employee interrupted and shall have the record of
the employee show same.
   Where the services of an employee have been terminated by the City for
economic reasons and the employee continued to perform services for the City
although paid under a state or federal program, such as the Emergency
Employment Act of 1971, and the employee is subsequently rehired by the City
during or immediately at the expiration of the state or federal employment, the
time so spent in the state or federal employment shall be included as part of
length of service with the City and shall not constitute an interruption of
City service for any purpose within this chapter.
   Where an individual has been employed and paid under a state or federal
program, such as the Emergency Employment Act of 1971, and has been assigned to
perform services for the City although not a City employee and the individual
is subsequently hired by the City during or immediately at the expiration of
the state or federal employment, the time so spent in the state or federal
employment while assigned to the City shall be included as part of length of
service with the City for any purpose within this chapter.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XIV,
Requirements as to Continuity of Service.
(Ord. 12-93. Passed 5-17-93.)
167.25 SENIORITY.
   (a)   Definitions.
      (1)   "Seniority" means the length of continuous service with the City,
dating from the employee's most recent date of employment.
      (2)   "Job seniority" means length of continuous service in a given job
classification.
   (b)   Termination Procedure.
      (1)   When it becomes necessary through lack of work, funds or
operational efficiency to reduce the number of City employees, which is hereby
determined to be a management right, employees shall be retained on the basis
of qualification, skill and ability as determined solely by the City.
      (2)   Employees shall be given at least two weeks' notice of layoff.
   (c)   Rehiring Procedure. In rehiring after a layoff, the City shall offer
re-employment to the extent to which additional help is needed to former
employees in the occupational classifications involved in the inverse order in
which such employees were laid off; provided however, that the employee is
qualified in the judgment of the City to perform the available work at the time
the offer of employment is made, and provided, also, that the period of layoff
does not exceed one year.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XXVII, Reduction in Force; Dispatchers, Article 18, Seniority.
(Ord. 4-04. Passed 1-20-04.)
167.26 STRAIGHT-TIME PAY FOR MEETINGS DURING REGULAR WORKING HOURS.
   (a)   All employees shall be paid at their established straight-time rates
for time spent during regular working hours at all meetings which the City
required them to attend. This, also, includes time spent at training and/or
seminars as authorized by the City.
   (b)   Members of the City Employee's Credit Union official family
representing the Credit Union, shall be paid at their established straight-time
rates for time spent during regular working hours, not to exceed one day, at
the annual State Credit Union Conference, the purpose of which is ultimately to
benefit City employees, when such attendance is authorized by the City Manager.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XV,
Straight Time Pay for Meetings.
(Ord. 12-93. Passed 5-17-93.)
167.27 MINIMUM TIME WHEN SCHEDULED WORK IS NOT AVAILABLE.
   (a)   Hourly-rated employees who report for work on time on a regularly
scheduled workday in the normal work week shall be paid eight hours at
straight-time pay for that day in the event scheduled work is not available.
   (b)   Hourly rated employees who are scheduled to work on their normally
scheduled days off and who report for work at the scheduled time shall be paid
three hours at straight-time pay in the event scheduled work is not available,
unless notified not to report for the scheduled work by quitting time on the
shift immediately prior to the normally scheduled day off.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XIII, Overtime and Pay Types; Dispatchers, Article 13, Overtime and Premium
Pay.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.28 MINIMUM TIME FOR EMERGENCY CALL-OUTS.
   Hourly-rated employees, salaried employees assigned to Class Grade 18 or
below and police and firefighting personnel assigned to Salary Grade 20 or
below, who are called out to perform emergency overtime work or for necessary
court appearances, shall be paid for each such call-out not less than the
equivalent of three hours at time and one-half.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XIII, Overtime and Pay Types; Dispatchers, Article 13, Overtime and Premium
Pay.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.29 MINIMUM TIME FOR STAND-BY.
   Hourly-rated employees and salaried employees assigned to Class Grade 18 or
below who are ordered to stand by for possible call-outs shall be paid for each
such eight-hour period required to stand by, two hours at time and one-half.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XIII, Overtime and Pay Types; Dispatchers, Article 13, Overtime and Premium
Pay.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.30 OVERTIME WORK.
   (a)   Overtime Administration. In any emergency, a department head may
prescribe, with the approval of the City Manager, reasonable periods of
overtime work to meet operational needs. Such overtime shall be reported and
justified as required by the City Manager.
   (b)   Overtime Pay.
      (1)   Employees paid on an hourly-rated basis shall be paid at one and
one-half times their regular hourly rate for any hours worked beyond forty
hours per week or eight hours per day, when authorized in accordance with
subsection (a) hereof.
      (2)   Salary-rated employees paid in Class Grade 18 or below, who are
eligible for overtime pay shall be paid at one and one-half times their regular
hourly rate as defined in the Compensation Schedules of the City for any hours
worked beyond forty hours per week or eight hours per day, when authorized in
accordance with subsection (a) hereof.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XIII, Overtime and Pay Types; Dispatchers, Article 14, Overtime and Premium
Pay.
   (c)   Overtime Compensation for Salaried Employees in Class Grade 19 or
Above. Salaried employees in the Administration Class (department/division
heads and senior supervisors) shall not be eligible for overtime compensation,
but may be granted compensatory time off by the City Manager in exceptional
cases and when conditions permit.
   (d)   Overtime Pay for Meetings Beyond Regular Working Hours. Salary-rated
employees in Class Grade 18 or below shall be paid at their established
overtime rates for time spent beyond regular working hours at staff or planning
meetings called by the City Manager or the responsible department head, or at
meetings of all agencies, boards or commissions when called by the presiding
officer thereto, when authorized in accordance with subsection (a) hereof.
   (e)   Determining Hours Worked for Overtime Qualification. For the purposes
of determining hours worked to qualify for the overtime payment calculation,
the following shall apply:
      (1)   Work week schedule. The normal work week schedule shall not be the
determinate, rather it is when the employee goes beyond forty hours in a week.
(For these purposes there shall be no duplicating, pyramiding or doubling of
hours.)
      (2)   Holidays. A holiday shall be considered a day worked for purposes
of determining eligibility for overtime hours worked beyond forty hours per
week. Pay for overtime hours worked and/or work on a holiday shall not be
duplicated, pyramided or counted again for the purpose of computing overtime
pay.
      (3)   Vacation. Vacation time shall be considered as time worked for
purposes of determining eligibility for overtime pay for hours worked beyond
forty hours per week. Pay for overtime hours worked and/or work on a vacation
day shall not be duplicated, pyramided or counted again for purposes of
computing overtime pay.
      (4)   Sick leave. Sick leave hours taken shall be considered as time
worked for the purpose of determining eligibility for overtime pay hours worked
beyond forty hours per week. These hours, as well as hours in subsection (e)(3)
hereof, may only be considered if they occur within the body of the work week
and in no instance can they be used for this purpose on the "tail end" of any
week, or paid at an overtime rate for time spent away from work.
      (5)   Absence. Any other absence not provided for above shall not be
construed as time worked for purposes of determining eligibility for overtime
pay hours worked beyond forty hours per week.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XIII, Overtime and Pay Types; Dispatchers, Article 13, Overtime and Premium
Pay.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.31 REST PERIOD AFTER SIXTEEN HOURS WORK.
   (a)   Eligibility for Best Period, No Lost Time. Hourly-rated employees and
salary-rated employees who are eligible for overtime, who are required to work
in excess of sixteen hours within a twenty-four hour period, shall be entitled
to an eight-hour rest period before returning to work on a regularly scheduled
workday. In the event this rest period extends into the next regularly
scheduled workday within the normal work week, employees shall lose no time
thereby.
   (b)   Double-Time For Work During Rest Period. In the event employees are
required to work during the rest period set forth above, such employees shall
be paid double-time for all such hours worked during this rest period and for
all succeeding hours until relieved from further duty.
   Union Employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XIII, Overtime and Pay Types; Dispatchers, Article 13, Overtime and Premium
Pay.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.32 EMERGENCY COMPENSATION FOR SALARY-RATED EMPLOYEES IN CLASS GRADE 19 OR
ABOVE.
   In the event of an extreme emergency, the City Manager is hereby authorized
to approve additional compensation at the rate of twenty dollars ($20.00) per
hour to salary-rated employees in executive, administrative and professional
classes assigned to Class Grade 19 or above for work performed over and above
their normal responsibilities.
(Ord. 12-93. Passed 5-17-93.)

167.34 UNIFORMS AND EQUIPMENT.
   (a)   Employees shall operate City vehicles in a safe manner. Any accident
which occurs as the result of careless or negligent operation and/or behavior
of the employee shall result in disciplinary action up to and including
termination.
   (b)   The willful destruction of the employer’s, customers’, fellow
employees’ or public property shall result in disciplinary action up to and
including termination.
   (c)   The use of City owned or operated vehicles and/or equipment for
personal use and/or non-City related matters shall result in disciplinary
action up to and including termination.
   (d)   The City shall furnish proper tools and equipment necessary to do the
work and maintain the standard of service required by the City. When tools and
equipment are furnished by the City to the employee, the employee shall be
responsible for their return in good condition.
   (e)   The City will furnish to all Bargaining Unit employees requiring them,
uniforms and safety shoes to be worn in the manner as per the respective
Collective Bargaining Agreements. The City shall furnish to all department
heads, division heads and supervisory personnel, upon the approval of the City
Manager, uniforms and safety shoes to be worn at all times.
   (f)   Each salaried appointee of the Safety Department required to wear a
regulation uniform while on duty, shall be paid a uniform maintenance
allowance, in accordance with the following provisions:
 
      Group and Rate Designation
      Class Title              Annual Rate
      Police Chief                   $ 800.00
           Fire Chief                
      Police Office Supervisor       600.00
      Auxiliary Police Officer       175.00
 
      (2)   Each specifically designated group above shall be paid a monthly
rate for each month or fraction thereof from the first anniversary of original
employment to the December 31 following such anniversary, payable at the end of
such December.
      (3)   Each specifically designated group above shall be paid the annual
rate indicated, at the end of each December thereafter, for each full calendar
month of employment during the year. For this purpose, leave of absence without
pay shall not be included in determining a full month of employment.
      (4)   In the event that employment is terminated thereafter for any
reason, the cumulative earned uniform maintenance allowance shall be paid on
the pay date immediately following the payment of earnings for the last
regularly scheduled pay period, to each specifically designated group above at
the monthly rate indicated per full calendar month of employment from January 1
of that year to the date of termination.
         (Ord. 15-02. Passed 6-17-02; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06; Ord. 29-24.
Passed 8-19-24.)
167.35 EDUCATIONAL REIMBURSEMENT.
   (a)   The City shall reimburse the employee for the cost of tuition, books
and appropriate fees associated with an approved course of study pertaining to
the employee's job, in accordance with the following provisions:
      (1)   The course of study shall relate to the employee's current position
or prepare the employee for promotion within his/her present area of work.
      (2)   The course of study shall be approved prior to beginning course
work by the department head and the City Manager.
      (3)   Reimbursement shall be made for tuition, books and appropriate fees
associated with an approved course, and shall only be made after the Finance
Department has received notice of the official grade, indicating satisfactory
completion of the course of study, along with a receipt for the tuition, books
and such appropriate fees associated with the approved course of study. Such
reimbursement shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) per calendar year.
   (b)   The City shall reimburse the employee for costs associated with the
taking of license and certification exams, provided the employee receives a
passing grade. The employee shall pay all license and certification renewal
fees.
   (c)   When an employee assigned to a class requiring a license or
certificate for qualification has qualified for a higher level license than
required for his/her classification, or even though the specific position of an
employee may not require a license or certificate and the employee obtains the
same, the employee shall be eligible for additional compensation at the rate of
twenty dollars ($20.00) per month for as long as the license is held and is
valid. This payment shall be only for one license of a higher level.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XXIV, Educational Reimbursement.
(Ord. 6-99. Passed 4-19-99.)
167.36 HOLIDAYS.
   All full-time non-bargaining unit employees shall receive their regular
compensation for the following holidays, or part thereof. If a holiday falls on
an employee’s regularly scheduled day off, he shall celebrate such holiday on
his closest regularly scheduled working day after the holiday. If an employee
is required to work on such holiday, he/she shall be paid at the rate of eight
hours straight time for the holiday, and time and one-half for all hours worked
on that holiday, and there shall be no other compensating day off.
   (a)   The following are the approved holidays:
      (1)   The first day of January (New Year’s Day).
      (2)   The third Monday of January (Martin Luther King, Jr. Day).
      (3)   The third Monday of February (Presidents’ Day).
      (4)   The last Monday of May (Memorial Day).
      (5)   The nineteenth of June (Juneteenth).
      (6)   The fourth day of July (Independence Day).
      (7)   The first Monday of September (Labor Day).
      (8)   The eleventh day of November (Veterans’ Day).
      (9)   The fourth Thursday of November (Thanksgiving Day).
      (10)   The twenty-fourth day of December (Christmas Eve).
      (11)   The twenty-fifth day of December (Christmas Day).
      (12)   The employee’s choice (Employee shall notify his/her supervisor no
less than one week nor more than one month before the selected date in order
that this day may be approved in advance).
      (13)   A personal holiday, to be taken at the employee’s discretion
(Employee shall notify his/her supervisor no less than one week nor more than
one month before the selected date in order that it might be approved in
advance; however except that if the City Manager should declare that day at the
beginning of the year to be a given day, then all employees shall celebrate
that designated day, unless scheduled to work, and in that case, straight time
shall be paid to all employees working and a compensating day off shall be
granted in accordance with the provisions set forth herein).
   (b)   An employee shall forfeit all rights to his/her holiday pay for any
such holiday if he/she has an unexcused absence on his/her last regularly
scheduled work day preceding such holiday, or on his/her first regularly
scheduled work day immediately following such holiday.
   (c)   In addition to the above, any day may be designated as a holiday by
proclamation of the President of Council upon approval of Council.
   (d)   Any employee regularly employed on a continuous work schedule of less
than full time shall be entitled to compensation for the above designated
holidays, based on the position’s budgeted number of hours prorated against a
full-time employee.
   All bargaining unit employees’ holiday benefits are outlined in their
respective Collective Bargaining Agreements.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97; Ord. 16-14. Passed 11-3-14; Ord. 28-22. Passed
12-21-22.)
167.37 USE OF EMPLOYEE'S MOTOR VEHICLE FOR CITY BUSINESS.
   (a)   City employees who use their own motor vehicle on City business shall
be paid for the use of such motor vehicle at the current IRS rate.
   (b)   No City employee shall use his or her own motor vehicle for City
business unless he or she is so expressly authorized by the City Manager. Any
employee using his or her motor vehicle on City business without the express
authorization by the City Manager shall not be compensated therefor.
(Ord. 18-97. Passed 7-7-97; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06.)
167.38 VACATION LEAVE.
   (a)   Eligibility.
      (1)   Regular, full-time employees shall earn and be granted, as provided
in Section
167.39, vacation leave with pay each calendar year for full-time service
performed with the City.
      (2)   Regular, part-time employees shall earn and be granted, as provided
in Section
167.39, vacation leave with pay each calendar year for service performed with
the City.
      (3)   No vacation leave credit shall be earned or granted for seasonal
employees in the City service or individuals holding volunteer positions as
Special Police Officers, School Crossing Guards or part-time Firefighters.
      (4)   Vacation leave shall be exclusive of authorized holidays.
   (b)   Qualifications.
      (1)   In the case of initial employment, eligible employees shall be
entitled to use such vacation leave credit earned.
      (2)   In the case of termination of employment, eligible employees shall
be granted any earned unused current vacation leave in accordance with the
provisions for scheduling payment of termination benefits as outlined elsewhere
in this chapter.
      (3)   An employee retiring or voluntarily terminating employment may
elect to use earned unused current years’ vacation leave and/or accrued
vacation leave as scheduled time off prior to the date of retirement or
termination. In this event, the vacation leave shall be actually scheduled and
taken prior to the date of retirement or voluntary termination. Such election
shall not extend the date of termination of employment with the City.
      (4)   An employee of the City, earning vacation leave credit currently,
is entitled to have prior service with the State, or any political subdivision
of the State, including prior City service, counted as service with the City,
for the purpose of computing the amount of vacation leave credit. Such credit
will be applied January 1 of the year following the completion of probation.
      (5)   An employee whose employment is terminated within one year of
initial employment, for any reason, shall not be granted vacation leave.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XVIII, Vacation Leave.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97; Ord. 12-13. Passed 9-16-13.)
167.39 COMPUTATION OF VACATION LEAVE CREDIT.
   (a)   Regular, Full-Time Employees. Each eligible employee shall be entitled
to vacation leave credit with pay, in active pay status, shall be granted the
following vacation leave with full pay for each year based upon their length of
service as follows. Should an employee have less than 80 hours in active pay
status, their vacation accrual will be prorated to reflect the percentage of
hours in active pay status, in accordance with the following schedule:
                      HOURS OF VACATION LEAVE CREDIT
Period of Continuous  Employees
Service With City     For Each Completed 80 Hours of Regular Time Service Per
                      Pay Period (Hours)
                           HOURS OF VACATION LEAVE CREDIT
Period of Continuous       Employees
Service With City          For Each Completed 80 Hours of Regular Time Service
                           Per Pay Period (Hours)
(1)   Less than one year3.08
(2)   Completed one year3.08
(3)   Completed five yea4.62
(4)   Completed 12 years6.15
(5)   Completed 18 years7.69
*As a result of initial employment, termination of employment, authorized
leave of absence without pay, seasonal employment.
 
   (b)   Accumulation of Vacation Credit During Authorized Absences. Employees
absent from work on authorized holidays, during sick leave, vacation,
disability leave, on special leave of absence with pay, or on special leave of
absence without pay, not to exceed three days in any one calendar year, shall
continue to accumulate vacation credit at the regularly prescribed rate during
such absence as though they were present for duty.
   (c)   Regular, Part Time Employees. Each eligible employee shall be entitled
to vacation leave credit for the time actually worked at the same rate as that
granted to employees under subsection (a) hereof.
   (d)   Effective Date of Vacation Leave Credit. Eligible employees who are
actively employed on their fifth, twelfth or eighteenth anniversary date of
employment with the City, shall have the vacation leave credit referred to in
divisions (a)(3) to (a)(5) hereof, applied retroactively to the first pay
period of such anniversary year.
   (e)   Round to Whole Hours. As of December 31 of each year, all vacation
leave credit earned for a full calendar year shall be rounded to the nearest
whole hour.

167.40 VACATION LEAVE IN EVENT OF DISABILITY.
   Absence on account of sickness, injury or disability in excess of that
hereinafter authorized for such purpose may, at the request of the employee and
within the discretion of the department head, be charged against vacation leave
allowance.
(1967 Code § 30.44)
167.41 SCHEDULING OF VACATION LEAVE.
   (a)   Each department head shall keep necessary records of vacation leave
allowance and shall schedule vacation leaves with particular regard to
seniority of employees and in accordance with operating requirements, and
insofar as possible, with the written requests of employees.
   (b)   When vacation leave is used, it shall be deducted from the employee’s
credit on the basis of one-half hour for every one-half hour, or fraction
thereof, of absence from the normal work day.
   (c)   (1)   With the approval of the department head and the City Manager,
an employee may carry forward, from one year to the next, unused vacation leave
not to exceed three weeks. However, the City Manager has the authority to
approve additional carryover time with a written request and review.
      (2)   The City Manager may elect to compensate department/division heads
and senior supervisors and City Council may elect to compensate the City
Manager for up to one week of unused vacation when circumstances associated
with City operations prevent or make it undesirable for such vacation to be
taken provided the employee carries forward the maximum number of weeks of
unused vacation permitted by this section.
   (d)   An employee retiring or terminating employment with the City, may
elect to receive unused earned vacation leave, as termination pay rather than
scheduling such vacation leave during the period prior to the date of
retirement or termination.
(Ord. 35-01. Passed 12-3-01; Ord. 9-18. Passed 7-16-18; Ord. 2-19. Passed 1-22-
19.)
167.42 SICK LEAVE.
   (a)   Full-Time Employees. Each full-time employee of the City shall be
entitled, for each completed eighty hours of regular time service per pay
period, to sick leave credit of 4.60 hours with pay.
   (b)   Part-Time Employees. Part-time employees shall be entitled to sick
leave for the time actually worked at the same rate as that granted full-time
employees.
   (c)   Accumulation. Unused sick leave credit shall be cumulative without
limit.
   (d)   Authorized Absences. Employees absent from work on authorized
holidays, during sick leave, vacation, paid disability leave, on special leave
of absence with pay or on special leave of absence without pay, not to exceed
three days in any calendar year, shall continue to accumulate sick leave credit
at the regularly prescribed rate during such absence as though they were
present for duty.
   Union Employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XVI,
Sick Pay; dispatchers, Article 16, Sick Leave.
(Ord. 8-98. Passed 4-6-98.)
167.43 USE OF SICK LEAVE.
   An employee eligible for sick leave with pay may use such sick leave, upon
approval of the City Manager, only for absence due to illness, injury, exposure
to contagious disease which could be communicated to other employees,
authorized maternity/adoption leave and illness or death in the employee's
immediate family.
   In the event of illness in the employee's immediate family, such use of sick
leave shall be restricted to those instances where the member of the immediate
family is a spouse, child or parent.
   In the event of death in the employee's family, bereavement leave of three
working days is authorized by Section
167.481. In the further event of extenuating circumstances, sick leave may be
charged, not to exceed an additional two working days.
   The employee's immediate family means: spouse, child, grandchild, mother,
mother-in-law, father, father-in-law, sister, sister-in-law, brother, brother-
in-law, daughter-in law, son-in-law, grandparents, grandparent-in-law and the
legal guardian or other person who stands in place of a parent (loco parentis).
(Ord. 18-97. Passed 7-7-97.)
167.44 NOTIFICATION BY EMPLOYEE.
   An employee on an assigned shift, reporting off work due to illness, shall
notify the shift supervisor at least thirty minutes prior to his starting time
on each day he is absent. When the employee has been absent for all or part of
his shift, he shall be considered on sick leave until he notifies the shift
supervisor that he will report on his next regularly scheduled shift, and such
notification shall be at least four hours prior to the starting time of that
shift. If circumstances are such that the employee has been unable to make this
notification before the four-hour time limit, and at the time that he does
contact his shift supervisor arrangements for filling his job have not been
completed, the employee shall be allowed to report to work, provided he states
he will come in on time, and any other conditional releases have been met.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XVI,
Sick Pay; Dispatchers, Article 16, Sick Leave.
(Ord. 12-93. Passed 5-17-93.)
167.45 SICK LEAVE FOR PART OF A DAY.
   (a)   When sick leave is used, it shall be deducted from the employee’s
credit on the basis of one-half hour for every one-half hour, or fraction
thereof, of absence from previously scheduled work.
   (b)   Should an employee have less than 80 hours in active pay status, their
sick leave accrual will be prorated to reflect the percentage of hours in
active pay status. Unused sick leave shall continue to accumulate without
limitations.
(Ord. 11-78. Passed 4-17-78; Ord. 9-18. Passed 7-16-18; Ord. 2-19. Passed 1-22-
19.)
167.46 PAYMENT OF ACCUMULATED SICK LEAVE UPON RETIREMENT.
   (a)   Upon the retirement of the employee or disability retirement of the
employee, and the employee has completed ten years of service, such employee
shall be entitled to receive a cash payment equal to his or her basic rate of
pay at the time of the above listed condition multiplied by 33-1/3% of the
total number of accumulated unused sick hours earned by the employee up to
1,500 and 33-1/3% for all accumulated and unused sick hours earned by the
employee in excess of 1,500 hours.
   (b)   For the purpose of this section, "retirement" means termination of
full-time, active service with the City to immediately accept pension benefits
for which the employee is qualified at the retirement date, from either the
Public Employees Retirement System of Ohio or the Police and Firemen's Pension
and Disability Fund of the State of Ohio, or other state pension fund.
   (c)   In the event of the death of an employee still in City service who has
met the time requirements specified in subsection (a) hereof, the payment as
described above shall be paid to the employee's estate.
   (d)   In addition to the above, a full-time City employee (in good standing
from active service), upon resignation, shall be paid for the value of earned
and accrued but unused sick leave earned while in the employ of the City in
accordance with the following schedule:
      (1)   After ten years of service, using the formula in subsection (a)
hereof, 25% of the adjusted balance, to a maximum of ten days will be paid.
      (2)   After 15 years of service, using the formula in subsection (a)
hereof, 50% of the adjusted balance, to a maximum of 20 days will be paid.
      (3)   After 20 years of service, using the formula in subsection (a)
hereof, 75% of the adjusted balance, to a maximum of 30 days will be paid.
      (4)   After 25 years of service, using the formula in subsection (a)
hereof, 100% of the adjusted balance, to a maximum of 40 days will be paid.
   (e)   In the event that an "on-duty" injury results in the death of an
employee as determined by the respective state pension fund, the City shall pay
the deceased's estate the current value of accumulated, unused sick time.
(Ord. 6-99. Passed 4-19-99; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06.)
167.47 PROOF OF ILLNESS.
   (a)   An employee on sick leave shall furnish a written, signed statement to
justify the use of sick leave.
   (b)   If medical attention is required, a certificate stating the nature of
the illness from a licensed physician shall be required to justify the use of
sick leave.
   (c)   If absence due to illness or injury exceeds three working days, a
certificate stating the nature of the illness or injury from a licensed
physician shall be required to justify the use of sick leave. For this purpose,
normally scheduled days off each week, or holidays, shall not be considered in
determining the three working days. If the illness or injury continues more
than seven calendar days, weekly written reports from the physician shall be
presented.
   (d)   If, the City Manager believes there is reason to doubt the employee's
actual sickness, the City Manager may require evidence thereof and if such
evidence would not convince a reasonable man of the fact of the illness, sick
pay shall not be allowed.
   (e)   Appropriate forms for the above statements and certificates shall be
furnished by the City Manager.
   (f)   Any employee fraudulently claiming sick leave, or a department head
falsely certifying to sick leave allowance for absence from work for other
reasons, shall be subject to disciplinary action, including suspension or
dismissal. This includes the falsification of either a written, signed
statement or the presentation of a false physician's certificate.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XVI,
Sick Leave.
(Ord. 8-98. Passed 4-6-98.)
167.48 REINSTATEMENT OR TRANSFER OF SICK LEAVE CREDIT.
   An employee who is laid-off from his position may, if reappointed, have
available for his use any unused sick leave existing at the time of his layoff.
An employee who transfers from one position to another, or from another public
agency in the State, shall be credited with the unused balance of his
accumulated sick leave, but not in excess of the accrual limit effective for
employees of the City.
(Ord. 53-74. Passed 12-30-74.)
167.481 BEREAVEMENT LEAVE.
   (a)   In the event of death in the employee’s immediate family, the employee
shall be granted bereavement leave of three working days, which must include
the day of the funeral, not to affect the employee’s unused sick leave credit
balance. This three days may be extended as set forth in Section (4) of the
sick leave provisions of this Agreement, Article XVI.
   (b)   For the purposes of bereavement leave, “immediate family” shall mean:
spouse, child, grandchild, mother, mother-in-law, father, father-in-law,
sister, sister-in-law, brother, brother-in-law, daughter-in-law, son-in-law,
grandparents, grandparents-in-law, legal guardian, or any person who stands in
the place of a parent (loco parentis).
   (c)   An employee may request up to three days of sick leave to attend the
funeral of the following: domestic partner, aunt, uncle, or cousin.
   (d)   The department head may, at his or her discretion, require
verification of attendance from the funeral director prior to granting/
authorizing such leave.
   Union employees, refer to your collective bargaining agreement, Article XIX,
Bereavement Leave.
(Ord. 6-99. Passed 4-19-99; Ord. 9-18. Passed 7-16-18; Ord. 2-19. Passed 1-22-
19.)
167.49 DISABILITY LEAVE.
   (a)   An employee receiving a job related injury shall be eligible to file a
Workers' Compensation Claim, and shall receive continuation of salary for up to
and including seven months. The claim shall be filed so as to allow for the
payment of medical bills. After seven months, the claim shall be filed as a
lost time claim, and wages paid to the employee shall then be offset by the
City against the moneys received by the employee from the Worker's Compensation
Bureau. This wage offset shall continue, and be in conjunction with the
previous wage continuation for up to one year from the date of the injury.
After one year, the employee shall then be eligible to use sick leave and/or
vacation in accordance with their available sick leave and/or vacation balance.
   (b)   Payment for lost time of one to seven days due to service connected
injury or illness shall not be taken from accumulated sick leave if it is
determined that the lost time would have been covered under the Workers'
Compensation laws if it had extended beyond seven days. To qualify for payment
under this provision, the employee shall require medical attention and a signed
certificate from a licensed physician shall be submitted along with a sick
leave form weekly to the City. Claims for treatment and medicine approved by
the Bureau of Workers' Compensation also shall be accepted as evidence of
service connected illness or injury.
   (c)   Subsequent medical attention after an employee returns to work from a
service connected injury or illness requiring time away from work shall be
charged to the employee's sick leave until such time as the Workers'
Compensation Bureau approves the claim for such medical treatment, and notice
thereof is provided to the City. At that point, the time taken from the sick
leave accrual of the employee shall be credited back to the employee as
appropriate provided the following conditions are met:
   The sick leave request submitted was accompanied by a certificate signed by
the attending physician and indicating the date of treatment; and a copy of the
Workers' Compensation form submitted by the physician to the Bureau for payment
to the physician is also attached. Should subsequent medical attention be
required after six months from the most recent medical treatment, an
application to reactivate the claim shall be filed through the Human Resources
office.
   Claims that are certified by the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation as an
aggravation of a preexisting injury and assigned the corresponding previous
claim number will be treated likewise by the City when determining whether the
injury is new for purposes of wage continuation for one year from date of
injury. Employees in a Bureau of Workers’ Compensation Rehabilitation Plan will
have their wages offset by the City for the duration of the plan.
   (d)   In the absence of proof of service connected illness or injury, the
employee's personal sick leave shall be charged. If personal sick leave credit
is not sufficient to cover the above described lost time, the absence not so
covered may be deducted from the employee's pay or charged to vacation time.
   (e)   The City may establish a modified work program designed to provide
temporary opportunity to those employees who are unable to perform their normal
work assignments due to an on-the-job injury. Implementation of the modified
work program shall be at the City’s option and shall be in strict compliance
with applicable federal and state Workers’ Compensation statutes. Employees on
modified work will receive wage continuation.
   The modified work assignment will be included in the calculation of lost
time for the purpose of determining the filing date for lost time claims with
the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation seven months from the date of injury. The
modified work shall be offered on a nondiscriminatory basis to those employees
who have sustained an on-the-job injury and who have received a medical release
from the attending physician setting forth the limitations under which the
employee may perform such modified work.
   Modified work shall be restricted to the type of work that is not expected
to result in a re-injury and which can be performed within the medical
limitations set forth by the attending physician. It is understood and agreed
that those employees who, consistent with professional medical evaluations and
opinion, may never be expected to receive an unrestricted medical release,
shall not be eligible to participate in a modified work program.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article XXI,
Workers' Compensation.
(Ord. 6-99. Passed 4-19-99.)
167.50 INCAPACITATION.
(EDITOR’S NOTE: Former Section 167.50 was repealed by Ordinance 18-97, passed
July 7, 1997.)
167.51 MILITARY LEAVE.
   (a)   In accordance with state law, any employee who presents official
orders requiring his/her attendance for a period of training or other active
duty as a member of the United States Armed Forces shall be entitled to
military leave without reduction in total income for a period or periods not
exceeding a total of thirty eight-hour working days in any one calendar year.
Such nonreduction in income shall be accomplished by the employee supplying to
the payroll office a copy of his/her military pay voucher, at which point the
City will then process the difference between the military pay voucher and the
normal wage due the employee for the time away, the amount to be paid in the
next processed payroll. Such military leave shall be in addition to and may not
be concurrent with authorized vacation leave. Any employee who enters extended
military service with the Armed Forces shall be granted leave of absence
without pay to extend until ninety days beyond the termination of such service.
   (b)   An employee who is reinstated to a position previously held by him
shall be entitled to receive compensation at a rate no lower than that of the
rate corresponding to the step rate received at the time of entrance into the
Armed Forces of the United States causing such separation.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XXII, Military Leave.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.52 SPECIAL LEAVE.
   (a)   The City Manager may authorize special leaves of absence with or
without pay for any period or periods not to exceed three calendar months in
any one calendar year for the following purposes: attendance at college,
university or business school for the purpose of training in subjects related
to the work of the employee and which will benefit the employee and the City
service; urgent personal business requiring the employee's attention for an
extended period such as settling estates, liquidating a business, serving on a
jury and attending court as a witness, and for purposes other than the above
that are deemed beneficial to the City service.
   (b)   Council, upon the recommendation of the City Manager, may grant leaves
of absence with or without pay in excess of the limitations above for the
purposes of attending extended courses of training at a recognized university
or college and for other purposes that are deemed beneficial to the City
service.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XXIII, Special Leave.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.53 MATERNITY/ADOPTION LEAVE.
   (a)   Employees of the City who become pregnant, or who are adopting a
child, and who desire to return to work at a future date, shall be granted
maternity or adoption leave. Such leave shall be for a period of up to three
months, which may be extended upon agreement by both parties. A maternity or
adoption leave shall be with pay, as deducted from the employee's available
sick leave credit balance.
   (b)   Application for maternity or adoption leave shall be in writing and
shall contain a statement of the expected date of birth, or in the case of
adoption, the date of obtaining custody, the date the leave is to commence and
the anticipated date of return to service. Such written request shall be
submitted sixty days in advance of the beginning of the leave. Upon return from
approved maternity/adoption leave at the time set forth in the application for
leave, the employee shall be entitled to reinstatement to the same position
which was held prior to the leave or to an equivalent position.
   (c)   An employee, who because of a miscarriage, other unforeseen
circumstances or a personal desire to return to service, and who is physically
able to resume her duties as before the stated "intended return", may present a
medical certificate from the attending physician indicating the employee's
ability to return at a date earlier than specified. If a position for which
such employee is qualified is or becomes available, the employee shall be
granted such position.
   (d)   The City requires certification from a medical doctor that an employee
is physically able to perform all normal duties and obligations upon the
intended date of return from a maternity leave.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XXIII, Special Leave.
(Ord. 6-99. Passed 4-19-99.)

167.57 COMPUTATION AND SCHEDULING PAYMENT OF TERMINATION BENEFITS.
   The payment of termination pay, consisting of eligible unused current year's
vacation leave, accrued vacation benefits and eligible unused sick leave shall
be made on the pay date immediately following the payment of earnings for the
last regularly scheduled pay period. Such payment shall not extend the date of
termination of employment with the City. Such payment shall be computed on a
forty-hour per week basis for all employees, excluding firefighting personnel,
whose records of sick leave and vacation leave credit shall not be converted to
such forty-hour basis for this purpose.
(Ord. 9-95. Passed 6-5-95.)
167.58 GROUP HEALTH, MEDICAL, HOSPITAL OR SURGICAL BENEFITS PLAN.
   Health insurance includes benefit programs providing medical, hospital or
surgical benefits, or any combination thereof, covering all full-time
employees. Employees may participate in the Joint Health Benefits Committee to
evaluate options, select plans to be offered, and address cost sharing issues
for insurance coverage. The Joint Health Benefits Committee shall be empowered
to make health care decisions on benefits, plan design, premium share and the
like, based on the amount of money contributed by the City as defined herein.
   (a)   Enrollment. Enrollment in the City's health insurance program is
limited to the following periods:
      (1)   Within 30 days of initial employment with the City;
      (2)   During the open enrollment period each year, effective January 1 of
each year; and
      (3)   As changes occur in dependent status due to marriage, childbirth,
divorce, etc., but only to add or delete dependents to the program as the
result of a bona fide dependent status change.
   (b)   Premiums. For the year beginning January 1, 2007, the City will
increase its contribution to the insurance package up to 5% over the total cost
in 2005, and up to one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) to reserve. For the
year beginning January 1, 2008, the city will increase its contribution to the
insurance package up to 5% over the total cost in 2007, and up to one hundred
thousand dollars ($100,000) in reserve. If there is a decrease in the cost of
health insurance, the committee will determine whether to increase reserves,
decrease premiums or obtain better benefits.
   (c)   Coverage During Leaves of Absence. Coverage while on a leave of
absence from the City is as follows:
      (1)   All paid leave of absence and employees approved for FMLA.
Participation and coverage will continue as if the employee continued working;
and
      (2)   All authorized unpaid leaves of absence. Participation and coverage
will continue through the month in which authorized unpaid leave begins. To
continue to participate thereafter, the employee must pay the appropriate
premium (COBRA).
   (d)   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement.
(Ord. 20-05. Passed 5-16-05; Ord. 35-06. Passed 11-20-06.)
167.59 GROUP ACCIDENT BENEFITS PLAN.
   (a)   The City Manager shall, in accordance with an authorizing resolution
of Council, periodically contract with an insurance company authorized to do
business in the State, for the issuance of a policy or contract of group
accident insurance benefits covering all full-time permanent employees of the
City, at the expense of the City. The coverage shall be limited solely to the
employee.
   (b)   The insurance policy or contract shall provide that any such covered
employee may elect to obtain either or both of the following benefits, solely
at the employee's own expense, by means of authorized payroll deduction:
      (1)   Coverage in excess of the basic amount provided by the City.
      (2)   Coverage for spouse and qualified children.
   Union employees, refer to your Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article
XXVI, Health and Welfare.
(Ord. 37-97. Passed 12-15-97.)
167.60 FLEXIBLE BENEFITS PLAN.
   Employees may elect to participate in a flexible benefits plan as qualified
by Section 125 of the Internal Revenue Code through the use of the payroll
deduction, which may result in a pre-tax salary deduction paid by the employee.
The flexible benefits plan shall be as established, negotiated, and approved by
the City Manager in compliance with all applicable state and federal laws, and
as authorized by Council.
(Ord. 11-01. Passed 4-2-01.)
TITLE SEVEN - Judicial
Chap.
181.   Municipal Court.
CHAPTER 181
Municipal Court
   EDITOR’S NOTE: The Painesville Municipal Court having territorial
jurisdiction within the City and within Painesville, Perry, Leroy, Concord and
Madison Townships, has been established under Ohio R.C. 1901.01 et seq. Ohio
R.C. 1901.25 provides that the Municipal Court may provide by rule how jurors
shall be chosen. Jurors’ fees in any criminal case involving the violation of a
City ordinance shall be paid out of the City Treasury. The Municipal Court,
pursuant to Ohio R.C. 1901.26(A), may establish a schedule of fees and costs to
be taxed in any action or proceeding, whether civil or criminal. Ohio R.C.
1901.31(F) provides that fines received for violation of Painesville ordinances
shall be paid into the City Treasury. Rule 13 of the Ohio Traffic Rules as
promulgated by the Ohio Supreme Court provides that a court shall establish a
traffic violations bureau and specifies certain restrictions as to the
designated offenses and schedule of fines to be accepted as waiver payment in
lieu of court appearance.
181.01   Petty cash fund.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Release of Court Clerk’s liability for loss of funds - see Ohio R.C. 131.18
et seq.
   Municipal court - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 1901
   Bond for Court Clerk required - see Ohio R.C. 1901.31(D)
   Notification to Director of liquor law convictions - see Ohio R.C. 4301.991
   Record of traffic violations - see Ohio R.C. 4513.37
181.01 PETTY CASH FUND.
   In order to enable the Clerk of the Painesville Municipal Court to make
daily deposits of the total daily collection of the Municipal Court funds,
there is hereby established a petty cash fund in the office of the Clerk of the
Painesville Municipal Court. The petty cash fund shall be in the amount of six
hundred dollars ($600.00), and shall be drawn on the General Fund.
(Ord. 28-99. Passed 12-6-99.)
