705.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms, phrases, words and
their derivations shall have the meaning given herein. When not inconsistent
with the context, words used in the present tense include the future, words in
the plural number include the singular number, and words in the singular number
include the plural number. The word "shall" is always mandatory and not merely
directory.
   (a)   "Alarm System" is a monitored system designed for the purpose of fire
and/or police notification in the event of an emergency.
   (b)   "City" means the City of Painesville.
   (c)   "Council" means the City Council of Painesville.
   (d)   "City Manager" means the City Manager of Painesville.
   (e)   "Contractor" means any company and/or person entering into agreements
with anyone or business to provide, install, and/or service fire and/or police
alarm systems or provide monitoring services.
   (f)   "False Alarm" means the activation of an alarm system through
mechanical failure, malfunction, improper installation, improper operation or
negligence of the owner or lessee of an alarm system of his or her employees or
agents. Does not include alarms caused by hurricanes, tornados, earthquakes or
similarly violent conditions or conditions clearly beyond the control of the
user, and does not include activation of an alarm system while the system is
being tested to determine whether or not the system is in proper working order,
pursuant to established procedures. Alarms used for medical reasons are exempt
from false alarm fees.
   (g)   "Person" means any person, firm, partnership, association,
corporation, company or organization of any kind.
   (h)   "Subscriber" means any person, firm or partnership of any kind
entering into an agreement to have a monitored alarm system installed and used
within their premises.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.02 REGISTRATION OF ALARM BUSINESSES; CONDITIONS FOR TERMINATION; FEES;
RENEWALS.
   (a)   Any individual, partnership, corporation or other entity engaging in
an alarm business in the City shall register with the Police Division.
Registration shall be made on an annual basis on or before January 1 of each
year, shall list such information as may be required by the Chief of Police and
shall include the following:
      (1)   The name, address, and telephone number of the alarm business, the
kind of entity it is (individual, partnership, or corporate) and the name,
address, and telephone number of the individual proprietor, partners, or
directors and principal officers, depending on the nature of the entity
applying;
      (2)   A description of the alarm systems and devices offered for sale or
lease to the public and a description of any services related to alarm devices
offered to the public;
      (3)   A list of all felony and misdemeanor convictions of individual
proprietors, partners, or directors and principal officers of the applicant
business, including date and location of each conviction;
      (4)   A statement as to whether or not the applicant has ever been denied
a license or permit in any jurisdiction to engage in the alarm business or has
had such a license or permit revoked;
      (5)   A statement as to the length of time the applicant has been engaged
in the alarm business and where engaged;
      (6)   A list of the names and addresses of employees of the applicant who
will be or are performing work for the applicant in the City, together with a
list of all felony and misdemeanor convictions of such employees; and
      (7)   In the case of an alarm business which monitors alarms, the names
and addresses of each of its alarm users in the City.
      (8)   In the case of persons selling, installing, and/or servicing fire
Protection systems, proof of State Fire Marshal Certification is required.
   (b)   Registration of alarm businesses may be terminated by the Chief of
Police in the manner hereinafter set forth if the licensee or any of its
owners, partners, principal corporate officers or other individuals having
authority and responsibility for the management and operation of the alarm
business in the City are found to have:
      (1)   Violated any of the provisions of this chapter or any rule or
regulation of the City, which violation reflects unfavorably upon the fitness
of the licensee to engage in the alarm business, as determined by the Chief of
Police;
      (2)   Knowingly and willfully given any false information of a material
nature in connection with an applicant for a license or a renewal or
reinstatement of a license or in a notice of transfer of an alarm business
licensed under this chapter;
      (3)   Been convicted in any jurisdiction of a felony or a misdemeanor if
the Chief of Police determines that such conviction reflects unfavorably on the
fitness of the applicant to engage in the alarm business; or
      (4)   Committed any act while the license was not in effect, which act
would be cause for the revocation of a license or grounds for the denial of an
application for a license.
   (c)   An initial registration fee of $50.00 is required with an annual
registration renewal fee of $10.00 per alarm business to be paid by January 1
of each year, and a $35.00 renewal fee if payment is made on or after February
1 of each year.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.03 REGISTRATION OF SUBSCRIBERS; FEES; RENEWALS.
   (a)   Every alarm user in the City shall register annually each subscriber
in use with the Police Department.
   (b)   Each subscriber registering in accordance with this chapter shall
provide the following information to the Police Division:
      (1)   The name, address, and telephone number of the protected home,
business, or other location;
      (2)   The name, address, and telephone number of the alarm company which
installed or maintains the registrant's alarm system;
      (3)   In the case of a business entity, the names, addresses, and
telephone numbers of three responsible employees of the business who can be
contacted by the Police Department if needed;
      (4)   Whether the system is a security and/or fire alarm system; and
      (5)   Proof of building permit to install required systems in businesses.
These systems include, but are not limited to, fire and smoke detectors and any
other fire prevention device required by the Chief of Fire. Permits are not
required for installations made in individual homes.
   (c)   An annual registration form for each alarm user shall be submitted to
the Police Department by January 31 of each year. If the form is submitted on
or after February 1 of each year a $35.00 renewal fee will be charged.
(Ord. 26-03. Passed 12-22-03.)
705.04 EQUIPMENT REGULATIONS.
   (a)   All equipment used in installations for which a permit is required
shall meet the applicable standards of the Underwriters Laboratories and/or the
National Fire Protection Association; and/or other recognized industry
standard. Applicant may be required to submit evidence of the reliability and
suitability of the equipment to be installed.
   (b)   The sensory mechanism used in connection with such devices must be
adjusted to suppress false indications of fire or intrusion, so that the device
will not be actuated by impulses due to transient pressure change in water
pipes, short flashes of light, wind noises such as the rattling or vibrating of
doors or windows, vehicular noises adjacent to the installation, pets, or other
forces unrelated to genuine alarms.
   (c)   All components comprising such devices must be maintained by the owner
or the lessee in good repair to assure reliability or operation.
   (d)   Each alarm equipment supplier that sells or leases to a person an
automatic protection device which is installed on such person's premises in the
City shall furnish that person with instructions as to the way the device
operates, along with maintenance instructions and necessary information for
registration requirements.
   (e)   Each alarm equipment supplier shall also furnish the Chief of Police
and/or Chief of Fire with a copy of the instructions as to the way the device
operates. If the Chief of Police and/or Chief of Fire finds such to be
incomplete, unclear, or otherwise inadequate, he may require the alarm
equipment supplier to have the same revised to meet with his approval and then
promptly have copies distributed to persons for whom installations of such
devices are made.
   (f)   Each alarm equipment supplier that sells or leases to a person an
alarm device which is installed on such person's premises in the City for which
a permit is required must provide for receiving calls for service, directly or
through an agent, on a twenty-four hour basis, seven days a week, and shall
respond to such calls within eight hours of the time that they are received.
   (g)   At the time of installation, each alarm equipment supplier shall
furnish to the person for whom the automatic protection device has been
installed, written information as to how service can be obtained at any time,
including the telephone number to call for service; and such person shall be
responsible for having the device repaired as quickly as possible after he
learns from his own sources or from notification by the City, that the device
is not working properly.
   (h)   The Chief of Police and/or Chief of Fire or any officer designated to
them shall have the authority, at reasonable times, and upon oral notification,
to enter upon the premises within the City, to inspect the installation and
operation of an automatic protection device or signaling device, the purpose of
which is to report an emergency to the Police and/or Fire Departments. A
competent employee of the alarm company, to ensure proper working order of the
system, shall inspect all monitored systems annually. Upon completion of the
annual inspection of the alarm system proof of said inspection shall be
provided to the Police and Fire Departments.
   (i)   All equipment, the use or installation of which is subject to this
chapter, shall be maintained in good operating condition; the Chief of Police
and/or Chief of Fire may require that repairs or inspections be made whenever
he has determined that such are necessary to assure proper operation.
   (j)   The alarm equipment supplier shall also be held responsible for any
and all unpaid fines or fees accrued and left unpaid by the alarm user for
false alarms.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.05 FALSE ALARMS.
   (a)   If the Police Department and/or Fire Department receives more than 3
false alarms from any system in any calendar year, from and after the effective
date of this section, a residential alarm user shall be charged $25.00 for the
4th false alarm, $25.00 for the 5th false alarm, $35.00 for the 6th false
alarm, and $50.00 for the 7th false alarm and subsequent false alarms within a
year. Businesses will be charged $25.00 for the 4th false alarm, $50.00 for the
5th false alarm, $100.00 for the 6th false alarm, and $200.00 for the 7th false
alarm and subsequent false alarms within a year. False alarms from systems used
for medical purposes are exempt from fees.
   (b)   If fines are not paid within grace period (60 days), notice will be
sent by certified mail to the user, ordering the use of the system to cease and
disconnection of all equipment except those required by State or Local Code for
purposes of safety or security. If disconnection does not occur, the Chief of
Police may send a notice via first class mail of refusal to respond to alarm
calls from the address of the violating alarm user until the fees are paid in
full.
   (c)   Any alarm system disconnected pursuant to the above may be reconnected
at the expense of alarm user, provided that the registration required by this
chapter is complete and all delinquent fines and fees are paid in full.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.06 LIABILITY OF THE CITY.
   The acceptance of any alarm system by the Chief of Police shall in no manner
place upon the Police Division, the Fire Division, or the City any additional
liabilities or attest to the quality or appropriate functions or effectiveness
of any system, other than those legally incurred with Municipal emergency
service functions.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.07 PROHIBITIONS.
   (a)   No person owning or operating an alarm business shall sell, or offer
or install an alarm system in any business, building, structure or premises in
the City without first completing the procedures set forth in this chapter.
   (b)   No alarm user shall have installed or operate an alarm system in any
business, building, structure, or premises in the City without first completing
the registration procedures set forth in this chapter.
   (c)   Local alarms shall not resemble the sound of any emergency vehicle
siren or civil defense alarm.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.08 NOTICE.
   (a)   The City Manager or his/her authorized representative shall make and
enforce such rules and regulations as he may deem necessary for the enforcement
of the provisions hereof, and for the proper determination and collection of
fees and the charges herein provided.
   (b)   This chapter shall not take precedence over State Fire Code.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
705.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter, except Section
705.05 is guilty of a minor misdemeanor. Each day's continuance of a violation
shall be deemed a separate and distinct offense.
(Ord. 13-03. Passed 8-18-03.)
CHAPTER 713
Detergent Sales
713.01    Definitions.
713.02    Labeling.
713.03    Limitations.
713.99    Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Labeling of hazardous substances - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 3716
   Water pollution control - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 6111
   Water quality standards - see OAC Ch. 3745-1
713.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter, the following words and phrases shall have the
meanings herein ascribed unless the context clearly states otherwise:
   (a)   "Synthetic detergent" or "detergent" means any cleaning compound which
is available for household use, laundry use, other personal uses or industrial
use, which is composed of organic or inorganic compounds, including soaps,
water softeners, surface active agents, dispersing agents, foaming agents,
buffering agents, builders, fillers, dyes, enzymes and fabric softeners,
whether in the form of crystals, powders, flakes, bars, liquids, sprays or any
other form.
   (b)   "Polyphosphate builder" or "phosphorus" means a water softening and
soil suspending agent made from condensed phosphates, including pyrophosphates,
triphosphates, tripolyphosphates, metaphosphates and glassy phosphates, used as
a detergent ingredient, but shall not include polyphosphate builders or
phosphorus which is essential for medical, scientific or special engineering
use under such conditions and regulations as may be prescribed, after hearing,
by the Health Commissioner.
   (c)   "Recommended use level" means the amount of synthetic detergent or
detergent which the manufacturer thereof recommends for use per wash load, at
which level the synthetic detergent or detergent will effectively perform its
intended function.
   (d)   "Machine dishwasher" means equipment manufactured for the purpose of
cleaning dishes, glassware and other utensils involved in food preparation,
consumption or use, using a combination of water agitation and high
temperatures.
   (e)   "Dairy equipment", "beverage equipment" and "food processing
equipment" mean that equipment used in production of milk and dairy products,
foods and beverages, including the processing, preparation or packaging thereof
for consumption.
   (f)   "Industrial cleaning equipment" means machinery and other tools used
in cleaning processes during the course of industrial manufacturing, production
and assembly.
(1967 Code Sec. 99.01)
713.02 LABELING.
   No person, firm or corporation shall sell, offer or expose for sale, give or
furnish any synthetic detergent or detergent, whether in the form of crystals,
powders, flakes, bars, liquids, sprays or any other form, in the City after May
1, 1971, unless the container, wrapper or other packaging thereof shall be
clearly labeled with respect to its polyphosphate builder or phosphorus
ingredient content clearly and legibly set forth thereon in terms of percentage
of phosphorus by weight, expressed as elemental phosphorus per container,
wrapper or other packaging thereof, as well as grams of phosphorus, expressed
as elemental phosphorus, per recommended use level.
(1967 Code Sec. 99.02)
713.03 LIMITATIONS.
   (a)   No person, firm or corporation shall sell, offer or expose for sale,
give or furnish any synthetic detergent or detergent containing more than eight
and seven-tenths percent (8.7%) of phosphorus by weight, expressed as elemental
phosphorus, within the City after September 1, 1971. No person, firm or
corporation shall sell, offer or expose for sale, give or furnish any synthetic
detergent or detergent which requires a recommended use level of such synthetic
detergent or detergent which contains more than seven grams of phosphorus by
weight expressed as elemental phosphorus, within the City after September 1,
1971.
   (b)   The concentration of phosphorus by weight, expressed as elemental
phosphorus in any synthetic detergent or detergent shall be determined by the
current applicable method prescribed by the American Society for Testing and
Materials (A.S.T.M.).
(1967 Code Sec. 99.03)
713.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates, disobeys, omits, neglects or refuses to comply with or
resists or opposes the enforcement of any provision of this chapter, except
when otherwise specifically provided, is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third
degree for the first offense, and a misdemeanor of the second degree for the
second and each subsequent offense in any 180-day period. A separate and
distinct offense shall be regarded as committed each day on which such person
continues or permits any such violation or failure to comply is permitted to
exist after notification thereof.
CHAPTER 719
Going-Out-of-Business Sales
719.01   License required.
719.02   Application for license.
719.03   Bond required.
719.04   License fees.
719.05   Revocation or suspension of license.
719.06   Time limits for licenses.
719.07   Additions to inventory prohibited.
719.99    Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Petty theft by deception - see GEN. OFF. 545.05
719.01 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person, firm or corporation in the business of the retail sale of goods,
wares or merchandise shall sell, offer for sale, announce or advertise for
sale, such goods, wares or merchandise when such sale is described or referred
to either directly or indirectly in form or in substance as a going-out-of-
business sale, removal, loss, termination, loss or expiration of lease, closing
out, liquidation, creditors, damaged goods, forced sale, distressed stock or by
any other term which shall reasonably lead the public to believe that the owner
or offerer of such goods, wares or merchandise either by choice or necessity
will no longer continue to engage in business, at the same location, without
first obtaining a license as hereinafter provided. Nothing in this section
shall be deemed to apply to any person, firm or corporation who sells, offers
for sale, announces or advertises for sale goods, wares or merchandise at a
reduction in price when such reduction in price is made in the normal course of
business operations; nor to any person executing a process or order of a court
of competent jurisdiction; nor to the creditor's sale conducted by a licensed
auctioneer which does not exceed one day's duration.
(1967 Code Sec. 112.01)
719.02 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   Each applicant for a license required by Section
719.01 shall make application therefor to the City Manager or person designated
by him, prior to the advertising or offering for sale of any goods, wares or
merchandise. Such application shall be on forms provided by the City Manager or
other person designated by him, which shall include in addition to the name and
address of the applicant, the name and address of the person, firm or
corporation in whose behalf such sale will be conducted if such is other than
the applicant; the date when such sale shall commence; the complete inventory
including the quality, kind, character and wholesale market value of the goods,
wares or merchandise to be offered for sale. Such information shall be prepared
in the following manner, unless otherwise prescribed by the City Manager or
person designated by him:
   (a)   A listing of all goods, wares or merchandise which have been in stock
fifteen days or longer prior to the date of such application;
   (b)   A listing of all goods, wares or merchandise received in stock within
the fifteen days immediately prior to the date on such application;
   (c)   A listing of all goods, wares or merchandise which have been or will
be ordered and placed in stock during the pendency of such sale; and
   (d)   Such other information relative to the business as may be deemed
necessary by the City Manager or person designated by him.
   If the inventory itemized in the original application is not disposed of
within the required time, the City Manager may, as hereinafter provided, renew
such license and the fee for such renewal shall be determined by the wholesale
value of the inventory itemized on in the application for license renewal,
which form shall be provided by the City Manager.
(1967 Code Sec. 112.02)
719.03 BOND REQUIRED.
   Each applicant hereunder shall execute and file with the City a good and
sufficient bond in the sum of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500),
except that such bond shall not be required when the wholesale market value of
the goods, wares or merchandise to be offered for sale is not in excess of five
thousand dollars ($5,000), with two or more sureties thereon who shall be
freeholders with the City, or with the surety thereon a surety company
authorized to do business in the State and which bond shall be to the approval
of the Director of Law, and shall be conditioned upon faithful observance of
all the conditions of this chapter and shall also indemnify any purchaser who
suffers any loss by reason of misrepresentations in a sale licensed hereunder.
The bond shall continue in effect for a period of one year. The licensee shall
notify the City Manager of any suit filed as a result of the operations hereby
licensed. Any purchaser claiming to have been damaged by misrepresentation in
such sale may maintain an action at law against the licensee making such
misrepresentations, and may join as party defendant the surety or sureties on
the bond as herein provided.
(1967 Code Sec. 112.03)
719.04 LICENSE FEES.
   Each application for a license or license renewal for any thirty-day period
or part thereof shall be accompanied by the following fee:
   (a)   If the wholesale value of the inventory itemized in the application
for a license or the renewal thereof is not in excess of five thousand dollars
($5,000), the fee shall be five dollars ($5.00).
   (b)    If the wholesale value of the inventory itemized in the application
for a license or the renewal thereof is more than five thousand dollars
($5,000), but not in excess of ten thousand dollars ($10,000), the fee shall be
ten dollars ($10.00).
   (c)   If the wholesale value of the inventory itemized in the application
for a license or the renewal thereof is more than ten thousand dollars
($10,000), but not in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), the fee
shall be fifteen dollars ($15.00).
   (d)   If the wholesale value of the inventory itemized in the application
for a license or the renewal thereof is in excess of twenty-five thousand
dollars ($25,000), the fee shall be twenty dollars ($20.00).
(1967 Code Sec. 112.04)
719.05 REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF LICENSE.
   The City Manager or person designated by him, upon recommendation of the
Chief of Police, or upon his own initiative, may at any time revoke or suspend
a license granted hereunder for any violation of this chapter or of any law or
ordinance relating to the conduct of such business.
(1967 Code Sec. 112.05)
719.06 TIME LIMITS FOR LICENSES.
   No such sale as referred to in Section
719.01 shall be licensed or permitted for a period of more than thirty days,
Sundays and legal holidays excepted. Such thirty days shall be consecutive
except as to Sundays and legal holidays; provided that if the licensee does not
sell the quantity of merchandise listed in the application for a license he may
make application for extension of such license to the City Manager or person
designated by him and if upon investigation the City Manager or such other
person designated by him is satisfied as to the truth of the statements
contained in the application for renewal, he shall issue a renewal license for
a period not exceeding thirty days. Provided, further, that a maximum of two
such renewals may be granted, except that if cause is shown to the satisfaction
of the City Manager or person designated by him, additional thirty day renewals
may be granted until all the disposable inventory listed in the original
application for a license is sold. No license shall be issued to any person,
firm or corporation to conduct a sale at the same location where the applicant
has terminated a prior sale licensed hereunder within a period of eighteen
months subsequent to the termination of such prior sale. Nor shall a license be
issued to a purchaser of stock at a sale licensed hereunder for a period of
eighteen months subsequent to such purchase if the purchaser continues to
conduct business under the same firm name as that used by the seller of such
stock without having adopted a reasonable means of advertising the change in
ownership to the public or where in fact no bona fide change in ownership has
taken place and such purchase was a sham transaction intended to deceive the
public. Nor shall a license be issued to any person, firm or corporation who
shall not have been for a period of sixty days next preceding such sale
continuously engaged in the City in the business of selling goods, wares or
merchandise at retail. No person who has been convicted of violating any of the
provisions pertaining to a sale licensed hereunder shall be issued a license to
conduct such a sale or be employed in any manner in the conduct of such a sale
for a period of two years subsequent to such conviction.
(1967 Code Sec. 112.06)
719.07 ADDITIONS TO INVENTORY PROHIBITED.
   No additions whatsoever shall be made to the stock of goods, wares or
merchandise set forth in the inventory attached to the application for the
license required hereunder, and nothing shall be offered for sale or sold at
any such sale which is in addition to the stock of goods, wares or merchandise
described in such inventory. Under no circumstances shall the inventory offered
for sale exceed fifty percent (50%) of the average inventory carried by the
applicant over the preceding five years or if the applicant has been in
business for a lesser period of time then the inventory offered for sale shall
not exceed by fifty percent (50%) the average inventory carried for the period
of time the applicant has been in business. Any abnormal purchases during the
year prior to the application for a license shall be cause for refusal to issue
the license.
(1967 Code Sec. 112.07)
719.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the third degree. Each separate sale or offering for sale constitutes a
separate offense.
CHAPTER 725
Junk Dealers
725.01   Definitions.
725.02   Junk business; license required.
725.03   License fee.
725.04   Vehicles used for the collection of junk; license fee.
725.05   Collection of junk for charitable purposes; license required.
725.06   Revocation of licenses.
725.07   Push carts prohibited.
725.08   Junk yard or junk shop to be in building or enclosed premises.
725.09   Storage of junk.
725.10   Premises to be kept clean and free from fire hazards.
725.11   Records required.
725.12   Inspections.
725.13   Determining whether regulations apply to particular activity.
725.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   State licensing and required fencing - see Ohio R.C. 4737.05 et seq.
   Receiving stolen property - see GEN. OFF. 545.18
725.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter the following terms shall have the meanings
respectively ascribed to them:
   (a)   "Junk" means any personal property which is or may be salvaged for
reuse, resale, reduction or similar disposition, or which is possessed,
transported, owned, collected, accumulated, dismantled or assorted for any such
purpose. Used household furniture or used wearing apparel, used articles made
of precious metal or metals, used jewelry, used tools and other articles or
personal property which are bought and sold as secondhand property and which
are not handled as what is ordinarily called junk or salvaged material, shall
not be included in the term "junk" as used herein. Without limiting the
definition of junk, the term includes used or salvaged iron, brass, lead,
copper and other base metal or metals, and their compounds or combinations,
used or salvaged rope, bags, papers, rags, glass rubber, lumber, bricks, tile,
pipe, cement blocks, building materials and similar articles and used machinery
and used construction equipment or property, and used motor vehicles which are
used, owned or possessed for the purpose of wrecking or salvaging parts
therefrom.
   (b)   "Junk collector" means every junk dealer who does not maintain or
conduct a junk yard or shop, but who in his own behalf buys, sells, exchanges,
collects, receives or accumulates or handles junk and uses in connection with
such business or activity, a motor vehicle.
   (c)   "Junk dealer" means every person who buys, exchanges, collects,
receives, stores or sells any article or articles herein defined as "junk".
   (d)   "Junk yard" or "junk shop" means any place at which a junk dealer
buys, exchanges, collects, receives, stores, accumulates, sells or otherwise
handles junk.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.01)
725.02 JUNK BUSINESS; LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall maintain or operate a junk shop or a junk yard or engage in
the business or activity of a junk collector or a junk dealer without first
having obtained a license therefor. Application for such license shall be made
to the City Manager or person designated by him, upon such blanks as shall be
prescribed by him. In making the application, the applicant shall state his
name, whether a person, firm or corporation, the place or places of business or
activity at which such is conducted and maintained, the kind of vehicle used,
should applicant be a collector of junk and such other information as may be
required by the City Manager or person designated by him.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.02)
725.03 LICENSE FEE.
   (a)   A separate application and license fee shall be required for each
separate location at which the applicant maintains a junk yard or junk shop.
   (b)   With the application, an applicant for a license to operate a junk
shop or junk yard, but not to collect junk, shall pay as the annual license fee
for each calendar year ending on July 31 of each year the sum of fifty dollars
($50.00).
(1967 Code Sec. 118.03)
725.04 VEHICLES USED FOR THE COLLECTION OF JUNK; LICENSE FEE.
   (a)   The license fee for a junk collector, whose principal place of
business is in the City and who collects junk by the use of a vehicle, shall be
five dollars ($5.00) for each vehicle per year.
   (b)   The license fee for a junk collector whose principal place of business
is outside of the City and who collects junk in the City by the use of a
vehicle, is fifty dollars ($50.00) per year for the first vehicle and ten
dollars ($10.00) per year for each additional vehicle used to collect junk in
the City.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.04)
725.05 COLLECTION OF JUNK FOR CHARITABLE PURPOSES; LICENSE REQUIRED.
   Individuals, individuals acting in behalf of organizations, or organizations
collecting junk for charitable or community service purposes shall likewise
secure a license to make such collections. However, in case of individuals
acting in behalf of organizations or in case of organizations only one license
shall be required and that license shall be issued in the name of the
organization, and which license so issued in the name of the organization shall
automatically permit the use of vehicles in the collection of such junk without
further license for the vehicle. However, no license fee shall be charged when
the use is for the purpose set forth herein.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.05)
725.06 REVOCATION OF LICENSES.
   Any license issued hereunder may be suspended or revoked at any time by the
City Manager or person designated by him for the violation of any of the terms
or conditions of these regulations or any other ordinance of the City, or any
law of the State or of the United States, and it shall be the duty of the Chief
of Police and all police officers to call to the attention of the City Manager
or person designated by him, any such violation on the part of the licensee or
any of his employees, agents or representatives. Any such suspension or
revocation shall be noted upon the license, together with a statement for the
reason thereof.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.06)
725.07 PUSH CARTS PROHIBITED.
   No junk collector or junk dealer shall collect junk by means or use of a
push cart.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.07)
725.08 JUNK YARD OR JUNK SHOP TO BE IN BUILDING OR ENCLOSED PREMISES.
   No person shall maintain a junk yard or junk shop in the corporate limits of
the City unless such business is carried on entirely inside a building or
buildings or unless the premises on which such business is carried on is
entirely enclosed by an opaque fence built in a substantial manner, at least
eight feet high; provided, however, that if any portion of the premises is
contiguous to a railroad right of way, that portion of the boundary line so
fronting on the railroad right of way may be enclosed with a cyclone type metal
fence at least eight feet high; and all of such fences must be approved by the
Building Official. Such fence shall be painted and shall be maintained and kept
in a neat, substantial and safe condition. Gates which will be considered a
part of such fence, for access to the premises, shall be swung inwardly and
such gates shall be kept closed when the premises are not open for business.
Such gates shall provide a clear opening of at least twelve feet to permit
entry of fire apparatus.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.08)
725.09 STORAGE OF JUNK.
   No junk shall be stored in the City unless the same is in a building or
enclosed yard. Such junk, whether inside a building or in an enclosed yard
shall be so piled or placed that adequate passageways are open.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.09)
725.10 PREMISES TO BE KEPT CLEAN AND FREE FROM FIRE HAZARDS.
   All premises used as a junk yard or junk shop shall be kept and maintained
in as clean, sanitary and neat a condition as such business will reasonably
permit. The person operating a junk yard or junk shop shall maintain the
premises so used so that rats, vermin and fire hazards are as far as
practicable reduced to a minimum. No rubbish, material or other accumulations
which are to be discarded by such junk dealer shall be burned on such premises.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.10)
725.11 RECORDS REQUIRED.
   It shall be the duty of every person operating a business or activity as
herein defined to keep a separate book or record, open to inspection at all
times, in which shall be written, in the English language, at the time of
purchase, exchange or receipt of any used or junk articles of property, a
description of the person from whom the same was purchased, exchanged or
received, and the date and hour when each such article was purchased, exchanged
or received. Every entry in such book or record shall be consecutively numbered
and shall be legibly written or printed.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.11)
725.12 INSPECTIONS.
   It shall be the duty of the Building Official, Chief of the Fire Department
and the Commissioner of Health, and each of them are hereby empowered, to
inspect all junk yards or junk shops in the City at such intervals as they or
either of them deem necessary. Such inspection shall be for the purpose of
seeing that such premises are operated in conformity with this chapter and are
kept in a safe and sanitary condition.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.12)
725.13 DETERMINING WHETHER REGULATIONS APPLY TO PARTICULAR ACTIVITY.
   Should any person contend that he is not subject to the provisions of this
chapter by reason of being engaged in some business other than those regulated
by this chapter, it shall be the duty of the City Manager or person designated
by him to cause an investigation of such business or activity to be made and to
determine from such investigation the nature and character of the business or
activity conducted by such person. Such determination of the City Manager or
person designated by him shall be final and a license or licenses shall be
required of such person in accordance with the determination of the City
Manager or other person.
(1967 Code Sec. 118.13)
725.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any term or condition of this chapter is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the fourth degree. Each day's continuance of a violation of this
chapter or a condition permitted to exist in violation thereof shall be deemed
a separate and distinct offense.
