955.01 REFUSE COLLECTION SERVICE.
   This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Municipal Refuse
Collection Ordinance of the City".
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms, phrases, words and
their derivations shall have the meanings given herein. When not inconsistent
with the context, words used in the present tense include the future, words in
the plural number include the singular number and words in the singular number
include the plural number. “Shall” is always mandatory and not merely
directory.
   (a)   “Ashes” means the residue of the combustion of any type of solid fuel
such as wood, coke, charcoal and like substances.
   (b)   “Brush” means tree trimmings too large to containerize including
branches not over four inches in diameter and forty-eight inches in length.
   (c)   “Building or construction waste” means waste materials and rubbish
resulting from the construction, alteration or repair of buildings and
structures such as walls, driveways, sidewalks and the like. Building or
construction waste may consist of wood, plaster, metal, cement, lime, brick,
mortar, concrete, lathing, roofing, earth, stone, slag, cinders and structural
material.
   (d)   “Bulk items” means nonrefrigerant appliances, furniture, mattresses
and carpets.
   (e)   “City” means the City of Painesville, Lake County, Ohio.
   (f)   “City Manager” means the City Manager for the City.
   (g)   “Contractor” means the current holder of the contract with the City
for the curbside collection and disposal of refuse.
   (h)   “Dead animals” means the carcasses of dogs, cats, horses, and all dead
animals of like size as distinguished from the carcasses of birds, small
animals, rats and mice.
   (i)   “Director” means the Service Director for the City.
   (j)   “Garbage” means putrescible animal and vegetable waste resulting from
the handling, preparation, cooking and consumption of food.
   (k)   “Industrial wastes” means wastes that result from manufacturing,
industrial and wholesale businesses.
   (l)   “Multiple family residence or apartment” includes the grouping
together under a common roof or on a single lot of two or more residential
units.
   (m)   “Person” means any person, firm, partnership, association,
corporation, company or organization of any kind.
   (n)   “Public health nuisance” means either: (1) Any accumulation of solid
waste, refuse, filth, offal, garbage, or other unwanted or unused material
(other than toxic waste or hazardous waste as defined in R.C. Title 37) in any
location where such material may reasonably be expected to lead to the
accumulation of stray animals feeding thereon, or to the attraction of vermin
including rats, or to the creation of odors offensive to an ordinary person, or
to a deterioration of property values in the surrounding neighborhood; or (2)
the deposit of materials described in subsection (d) “bulk items” and
subsection (t) “unacceptable refuse” of this section on any tree lawn,
sidewalk, alley, or beside any public way in such a fashion that indicates an
expectation that such material is to be collected by the contractor for the
City or City of Painesville Public Works Department without paying or making
arrangements to pay the reasonable cost thereof.
   (o)   “Reasonable accumulation” means the amount of refuse determined by the
Director to be considered within reason during a collection period for the
standard charge.
   (p)   “Refrigerant item” means any appliance containing a chemical
refrigerant, including air conditioners, dehumidifiers, refrigerators and
freezers.
   (q)   “Refuse” includes all solid waste, except body waste, including
garbage, rubbish, ashes and street cleanings.
   (r)   “Regular collection” means the weekly scheduled and routinely
performed collection of normal accumulation of refuse.
   (s)   “Residential unit” means the place of abode of a person or persons
living separately or together as an independent family.
   (t)   “Unacceptable refuse” means automotive vehicle parts, tires, land
clearing residue (stumps, logs, etc.), animal excrement and dead animals,
building and construction waste, earth, large rocks, commercial waste and
industrial waste, hazardous waste or any refuse not properly bagged,
containerized or bundled.
   (u)   “Recyclable materials” means the following items for recycling:
newspaper, office paper (City Hall), glass, PET and HDPE plastic, aluminum, bi-
metal and tin beverage and food containers.
   (v)   “Yard waste” means grass, leaves, tree and brush trimmings.
   (w)   “Cost of abatement” shall, in the case of the removal of materials
described in paragraph (n)(2) of this section, be deemed to be that amount
which would have been payable for rubbish disposal at the location involved in
the abatement pursuant to Section 951.08, plus fifteen percent (15%) to cover
administrative costs involved in the collection of same; and in all other
cases, the actual cost of removal, including the hourly rate of pay of all
personnel involved, plus fifteen percent (15%) to cover administrative costs.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07; Ord. 28-25. Passed 9-2-
25.)
955.03 COLLECTION BY CONTRACTOR; REQUIREMENT TO HAVE TRASH SERVICE.
   (a)   The City shall contract for the service of refuse collection of
acceptable refuse from all detached residential units occupying a lot alone,
including two- and three-unit multiple family residences within the City. Every
residential household of one-, two-, or three-family dwellings each on a lot
alone shall have trash service through the City contractor and pay the City
contractor for the services provided, except those vacant properties (i) that
are registered with the City pursuant to the requirements of 
Chapter 1375 of the Codified Ordinances or (ii) for properties where the
property is not going to be occupied for a period of sixty days to 180 days and
the property owner has received written permission from the Service Director to
discontinue service for that period and the Service Director in that event
shall then notify the contractor by email that the service shall be
discontinued for the period of time designated by the Service Director.
   (b)   Collection of refuse from four-or-more-unit multiple family
residential, commercial, industrial, institutional or nonprofit locations shall
be by private haulers, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the date
scheduled for collection.
   (c)   Property owners of any detached residential unit occupying a lot alone
shall advise the contractor of their choice of service, the same for all units
upon said lot alone, from among the following options:
      (1)   Option 1 - Service Level A: Customers use specially colored/marked
bags purchased at designated locations. There shall be no limit on the number
of bags they may place out for collection, and no monthly charge for refuse bag
pickup service.
      (2)   Option 2 - Service Level B: Unlimited service. Customers use free
tote carts provided by the City's contractor or their own containers that meet
the specifications defined in Section 955.05(b). There shall be no limit to the
amount of refuse collected, provided the content complies with all other
provisions of this chapter.
   (d)   Owners of properties containing one unit, single-family residences may
choose either Option 1 or Option 2.
   (e)   Owners of properties containing two or three units on lots alone are
not eligible for the Option I Service Level A as identified above, but are
eligible for Option 2 Service Level B only for the residential units within
each structure.
   (f)   The property owner shall be responsible for the cost of service to all
units in one-, two-, or three-family dwellings, each on a lot alone, and shall
notify the contractor of dates of institution and/or cancellation of service
desired.
   (g)   No owner of any residential lot in the City that is improved with a
one-, two- or three-family dwelling shall fail to have trash service through
the City selected contractor. In the event any such residential owner's service
is terminated by the City selected contractor for non-payment, then such
termination of service shall constitute a violation of this section. Any owner
of any residential lot in the City that is improved with a one-, two- or three-
family dwelling that violates this section is subject to the penalties set
forth in Section
955.99.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07; Ord. 28-25. Passed 9-2-
25.)
955.04 COLLECTION SUPERVISED BY DIRECTOR.
   (a)   All refuse accumulated in the City shall be collected, conveyed and
disposed of either by the contractor or under special circumstances by the
City, under the supervision of the Director. The Director shall have the
authority to make regulations concerning the days of collection, type and
location of waste containers and such other matters pertaining to the
collection, conveyance and disposal as he or she finds necessary, and to change
and modify the same after notice as required by law, provided that such
regulations are not contrary to the current contract and/or the provisions
hereof. Waste of the categories listed under unacceptable refuse shall not be
collected, except under special circumstances as determined by the Director.
   (b)   Any person aggrieved by a regulation of the Director shall have the
right to appeal to the City Manager, who shall have the authority to confirm,
modify or revoke any such regulations.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.05 REFUSE CONTAINERS.
   (a)   Service Level A. Refuse containers shall be only approved bags readily
distinguishable by color and markings, which shall be purchased either from the
contractor, at the City Utility Office or at established outlets.
   (b)   Service Level B: Unlimited Service.
      (1)   Refuse containers shall be a refuse cart(s) (90 gallon) provided by
the contractor, and/or metal or plastic cans, equipped with suitable handles
and tight-fitting covers, and shall be watertight. Such metal or plastic cans
shall have the capacity of not more than thirty gallons each. Such containers
shall be of a type approved by the Director and shall be kept in a clean, neat
and sanitary condition at all times. Containers are not to weigh more than
seventy pounds when filled. Thirty-gallon plastic refuse bags may be used in
lieu of or in addition to containers or a refuse cart.
      (2)   Refuse containers shall be provided by the property owner unless a
free refuse cart is requested of, and provided by the contractor. Containers
shall be maintained in good condition. Any container that does not conform to
the provisions of this chapter or that may have ragged edges or any other
defect liable to hamper or injure the person collecting the contents thereof
shall be promptly replaced at the direction of the Director or the contractor.
The contractor or the Director shall have the authority to remove noncomplying
containers in the next collection following the attachment of a written or
printed notice. The notice shall be affixed to the container at least one week
prior to removal.
      (3)   The contractor shall provide for the removal of refuse of any
amount that is placed in proper containers at the curbline, alley line or
prearranged collection location.
      (4)   Except after 7:00 p.m. on the day before the regularly scheduled
refuse collection for the premises involved and the day of collection, no
person shall deposit, store, cause or allow to be stored on premises under his
or her ownership or control, any ashes, garbage, refuse, recyclable materials,
rubbish or waste paper, bulk items, refrigerant items or yard waste, unless
such deposit or storage takes place behind the rear building line of the
premises or within an enclosed structure so as not to be visible from the
street or adjacent properties at ground level.
      (5)   Refuse containers for collection of refuse from four or more unit
multiple-family residential, commercial, industrial, institutional, or
nonprofit locations shall be provided by the owner, lessee, occupant of the
premises, or an independent refuse hauler. Containers shall be metal and/or
plastic with tight fitting lids or covers and shall be maintained in good
condition. Any container that does not conform to the provisions of this
chapter or that is insufficient in size to completely accommodate the refuse
generated from the premises shall be replaced within seven days of written
notification by the Director. Storage of containers shall be behind the rear
building line of the premises or within an enclosed structure so as not to be
visible from the street or adjacent properties at ground level.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.06 ACCUMULATION OF REFUSE.
   (a)   Persons using plastic bags for the storage of garbage shall store
plastic refuse bags in a location that is secured or within a container so as
not to be attracting rodents and animals.
   (b)   No person shall place any refuse in any street, alley or other public
place or upon any private property, whether owned by such person or not, within
the City, unless it is in proper containers for collection or under express
approval granted by the Director. Nor shall any person throw or deposit any
refuse on the banks of or in any stream, river or other body of water.
   (c)   No person shall cast, place, sweep or deposit anywhere within the
City, any refuse in such a manner that it may be carried or deposited by the
elements upon any street, sidewalk, alley, sewer, parkway or other public place
or into any occupied premises within the City.
   (d)   Any unauthorized accumulation of refuse on any premises is hereby
declared to be a nuisance and is prohibited. Failure to remove any unauthorized
accumulation of refuse within twenty-four hours after notice from the Director
and/or his or her authorized agent shall be deemed a violation of this chapter.
If such notice is not complied with within the time limit specified, the
Director shall cause such violation to be corrected and the actual cost of such
correction plus a fee of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) for inspection and
other additional costs in connection therewith may be billed to the property
owner. Failure to pay the total cost within thirty days after notice as set
forth above, shall entitle the City’s Finance Director to certify same to the
Lake County Auditor to be placed upon the tax duplicate of the property and
collected as other taxes are collected according to law.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07; Ord. 7-09. Passed 3-2-
09; Ord. 49-11. Passed 12-5-11.)
955.07 POINTS OF COLLECTION.
   Refuse containers, brush, yard waste and bulk items and refrigerant items
shall be placed at the street curb or in the tree lawn area. Brush and/or yard
waste removal is limited to small quantities, neatly bundled, containerized or
bagged, not over four inches in diameter or over 48 inches in length.
Containers, brush, yard waste and bulk items may be placed for collection at
other locations when approved by the Director as necessary for special
collection problems.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.071 TIME LIMITATIONS.
   (a)   Containers, brush, yard waste, bulk items and refrigerant items for
collection shall be set out prior to 7:00 a.m of the regular collection day,
but in no case shall they be set out prior to 7:00 p.m. of the previous
evening. Emptied containers shall be removed from the curbside or tree lawn
area no later than 7:00 p.m. of the collection day.
   (b)   Refuse shall not be collected earlier than 7:00 a.m. nor later than 5:
00 p.m. on any given day.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.08 FREQUENCY OF COLLECTION.
   (a)   Residential Collection.
      (1)   The City shall award its contractor the exclusive license or
privilege to remove refuse from all single-family residential units and two-
and three-unit multiple family residences, and no other person, firm or
corporation shall, during the period of the license, be permitted to affect
such removal.
      (2)   The contractor shall collect refuse from each defined service level
residential address on the same regularly scheduled day each week.
      (3)   The contractor shall collect all appropriate accumulation of refuse
in proper containers from each defined service level residential address in the
City.
   (b)   Institution of Service.
      (1)   Owners of single-family residential dwellings on a lot alone will
present in the City's Utility Office and provide pertinent information in
writing.
      (2)   Owners of two- and three- family units will provide the City's
Utility Office with a written request bearing his or her signature and all
pertinent information.
   (c)   Curtailment of Service. Residential collection service may be
discontinued by the property owner for the following reasons:
      (1)   Service Level B. Absence of resident.
         A.   Resident moves.
         B.   Resident on vacation. (Whole calendar months only.)
      (2)   Service Levels A and B. Change of service level. At least thirty
days prior to the next quarterly billing by the contractor, a property owner
shall notify the contractor of his or her desire for an alternative service
level.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.09 CARRY-OUT SERVICE.
   (a)   The contractor shall provide carry-out service for residents of one-,
two-, or three-family dwellings who are handicapped, disabled, impaired or
otherwise precluded from or physically incapable of placing refuse containers
from his or her individual unit at curbside, upon request to the City from the
owner of a qualifying property.
   (b)   The City shall notify the contractor, in writing, when carry-out
service is to be initiated or suspended for each specific handicapped, disabled
or impaired qualifying resident. There shall be no extra cost for such carry-
out service.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.10 BULK ITEMS.
   The contractor shall collect bulk items, that is, appliances (except
refrigerant items), furniture, mattresses and carpets for subscribers to all
levels of service on the same regularly scheduled collection day or a
subsequent day as may be approved by the Director. There shall be no extra
charge for this service.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.11 REFRIGERANT ITEMS.
   (a)   Refrigerant items as defined in Section
955.02 shall be picked up on the day each week designated by the Director.
   (b)   The property owner shall notify the contractor in advance, and make
arrangements for the pickup of a refrigerant item on the designated day. There
shall be no additional cost for this service.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.12 VEHICLES USED.
   The actual producers of refuse or the owners of premises upon which refuse
is accumulated who personally collect and dispose of such refuse, persons who
dispose of waste material not included in the rules and regulations, and all
other collectors of refuse who desire to haul over the streets of the City,
shall use a watertight vehicle provided with a tight cover, and so operated as
to prevent offensive odors from escaping therefrom and refuse from being blown,
dropped or spilled.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.13 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Director shall have the authority to make such other reasonable
regulations concerning refuse collection and disposal as he or she finds
necessary, subject to right of appeal as set forth in Section
955.04(b).
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.14 FEES.
   (a)   The fees for specially colored/marked collection bags and pickup and
disposal of refuse assessed owners of single-family and two- and three-unit
residences shall be as established through the periodic bidding for such items
and service. Fees shall be based on the contracted rates obtained, and shall be
subject to annual review by the City and amended as deemed appropriate.
   (b)   Each property owner shall be responsible to the City's contractor, and
shall be billed by same, for the cost of refuse pickup service to the property.
   (c)   A schedule of all fees shall be on file in the office of the City
Manager, the Public Service Department, the Finance Department and the posted
in the Utility Office at City Hall.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.15 BILLINGS.
   (a)   An initial list of residential units to be serviced, with names and
mailing addresses of relative property owners, shall be provided by the City to
the contractor upon ratification of the contract.
   (b)    The contractor shall directly bill owners of properties containing
one, two, or three residential units serviced with refuse collection, on a
quarterly basis, in advance, upon mutual agreement by the City and the
contractor.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.16 DELINQUENT ACCOUNTS; ABATEMENT OF PUBLIC NUISANCE.
   (a)   All accounts shall be considered delinquent if not paid on or before
the due date appearing on the bill. The contractor shall be responsible for
holding delinquent accounts as uncollected accounts receivable until such time
that the City collects the amounts certified to the Lake County Auditor.
   (b)   The contractor shall furnish to the City, by July 1 and January 1, of
each year, the names and addresses of accounts that are greater than 120 days
delinquent. The contractor shall provide continuous, non-stop service to all
delinquent and/or past due residential unit accounts. The Director of Finance
shall certify to the Lake County Auditor the delinquent charges, and shall
forward the money to the contractor. The contractor shall continue to provide
service to all residential billing units during the entire collection process,
unless the Director approves refuse service termination.
   (c)   If a delinquent account that has been so certified by the contractor
to the Finance Director, and/or acceptable arrangements have not been made for
payment thereof, such account is subject to discontinuation of refuse pickup
service as determined by the Service Director unless otherwise directed by the
City Manager. The contractor's service shall be resumed thereafter only on
payment of the accumulated unpaid fees for the period past due.
   (d)   If the owner, occupant or person otherwise in control of a residential
unit shall either fail to pay the rates due for solid waste collection as
established in this section (1) for two successive billing periods, or (2)
shall fail to provide evidence of vacancy in accordance with Codified Ordinance
Chapter 1375, it shall be presumed that a public health nuisance as defined in
Section
955.02(n) is being maintained at said residential unit.
   (e)   If the owner, occupant or person otherwise in control of a residential
unit creates a public health nuisance and if a public health nuisance is
declared by the City Manager or the Director as such term is defined in Section
955.02(n) and in accordance with subsection (d) hereof, the Clerk of the
Legislative Authority of the City shall certify the total costs of each
abatement activity, together with the parcel number or another proper
description of the lands on which the abatement activity occurred, the date the
costs were incurred for each abatement activity, and the name of the owner of
record at the time the costs were incurred for each abatement activity, to the
Lake County Auditor who shall place the costs as a charge upon the tax list and
duplicate. These costs that are certified to Lake County Auditor are for
abating the nuisance described in subsection (d) hereof pursuant to R.C. §
715.261(B)(1) and for the category of "nuisance" described at R.C. § 715.261(A)
(2)(c).
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07; Ord. 28-25. Passed 9-2-
25.)
955.17 SCATTERING OR PILFERING REFUSE.
   No person shall without the consent of the owner or person in charge
thereof, disturb, scatter, remove or pilfer any refuse placed for collection.
This provision shall not apply to any employee of the Department of Public
Service in the performance of his or her assigned duties, or any of its
authorized agents or to a private person or organization authorized to remove
such refuse.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.18 YARD WASTE.
   The City shall itself or by contract, provide for the collection and
disposal of leaves, brush and tree branches less than four inches in diameter
and forty-eight inches in length and holiday trees on specified days in the
manner designated by the Director.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.19 DISPOSAL OF RECYCLABLE MATERIALS.
   (a)   The City shall enter into an agreement with a contractor and/or other
governmental agency for the exclusive license or privilege to remove recyclable
material from collection bins placed at a site determined by the City, and no
other person, firm or corporation or governmental entity shall, during the
period of the license, be permitted to affect such removal.
   (b)   Residents shall deliver recyclable materials to the contractor's bins.
The bins shall be emptied by the contractor on regularly scheduled days of the
week in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the City and the
contractor and/or governmental agency.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)
955.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a minor
misdemeanor. A separate offense shall be deemed committed upon each day during
or on which the offense occurs or continues.
(Ord. 8-99. Passed 6-21-99; Ord. 24-07. Passed 12-3-07.)

CHAPTER 1105
General Provisions
1105.01   Title.

1105.03   Authority and jurisdiction.
